modules.name: Ground-floor activation and frontage composition
modules.design_question: How much street frontage is active, transparent, fine-grained, sheltered and deep enough to work, and how much is lost to blank wall, lobbies, loading and driveways?
modules.effort: About 8-10 person-days in full; annotation UI is the main cost; bike flag +1, lighting and active-class +1. 13 Nov slice (about 3): segment classes, entrance spacing, longest blank run, crossings. Glazing, depth, hours, canopies by 10 Dec.
inputs: Layer0.Massing: ground-storey volumes (mesh, z from 0 to first-floor underside) with a program tag per volume
Layer0.ProgramTags: office | residential | hotel | retail | cultural_civic | public | amenity | mechanical | core | lobby
SiteContext.StreetEdges (SITE): polylines typed arterial | retail_high_street | lane | mid_block | transit_plaza, plus bike_facility flag (none | painted | protected)
SiteContext.PolicyArea (SITE), user-chosen: Granville Street Plan area, DD character area (C-5, C-6, HA-1, HA-2) or other Downtown area; CDDG 4.18 refers to each

EdgeAnnotations (user-drawn): per facade segment category (active | semi_active | passive | blank | service), active_class (fine_grain | major), glazing ratio, entrances, egress doors, canopy geometry, active depth, opening hours, lighting flag, grille permeability
Optional: neighbouring frontages for continuity at corners
CLIM wind result at entrances and transit plaza (optional; absent = 'not assessed: wind')
outputs: FrontageSegments: GeoJSON FeatureCollection<LineString> {street_type, category, active_class, length_m, glazing_ratio, entrances_n, depth_m, hours}
ActiveFrontagePct and ActiveDepthOkPct: numbers per street edge
Entrances: Point[] {use, width_m, hours} (consumed by P06-M04 and P06-M05)
BlankRunMax_m, ServiceFrontagePct, WeatherProtectionCoveragePct, NightActivePct: numbers per street edge
MajorActiveSegments: list with a 'justify' chip each
VehicleCrossings: {street_id, kind: driveway | loading, over_bike_facility, width_m}[] (to MOBI and P06-M08)
GroundFloorChecks: Check[] {clause_id, source_id, status, value, wind_state: assessed | not_assessed} (consumed by P06-M08 and PRES boards)

parameters.name: Active-use share of street frontage
parameters.relationship: More retail, cafe, civic, transit-entrance or hotel-lobby frontage on streets, corners and plazas gives more activity and visibility, but leaves less frontage for cores, loading and back-of-house, which must move to lanes or below grade.

parameters.name: Entrance spacing (fine-grain frontage)
parameters.relationship: Smaller spacing (more doors) gives finer grain and more eyes on the street; each door uses frontage and adds tenancies. CDDG S3.1.1a: typically 8.0-12.0 m on non-residential active facades.

parameters.name: Unit (storefront) frontage width
parameters.relationship: Narrower units give more varied tenants and finer rhythm but less efficient anchors; CDDG expects 7.6-15.3 m fine-grain units, with large uses designed to be demisable later.

parameters.name: Fine-grain versus major active use
parameters.relationship: The glossary separates small units with frequent entrances from large uses (grocery, cultural venues, hotel lobbies). One spacing rule for both would wrongly flag civic anchors, so majors are listed apart with a justify chip.

parameters.name: Ground-floor glazing ratio
parameters.relationship: Higher transparent share of the ground band gives more visual permeability and surveillance, but more glare and heat gain and less display wall. CDDG says 'most', no percentage; bird-friendly treatment can offset transparency.

parameters.name: Active-use depth behind the facade
parameters.relationship: Deeper active space behind the glass gives real activity and views in, not a 1-2 m display strip or lobby sleeve, but costs net area and core flexibility. The 9.1 m preset borrows G2.10.2c as an analogue.

parameters.name: Lobby class, hours, lighting and separate entries
parameters.relationship: Hotel lobbies and transit entrances count active; office and residential lobbies default semi-active (team). Evening hours and integrated lighting extend activation (G3.1.1b); glare and spill are limited (G2.16.2); G2.11.1 asks separate residential entrances.

parameters.name: Blank-wall run length
parameters.relationship: Longer blank wall, grille or egress-door runs give fewer reasons to stop and lower perceived safety; driven by cores, substations, loading and parkade doors on streets. Gates and grilles count blank unless permeable at all hours.

parameters.name: Vehicle crossings and service-door frontage
parameters.relationship: Each driveway or loading door on a street replaces active frontage and adds pedestrian-vehicle conflict; lane access removes both. Vancouver policy is to minimise driveway width and number across sidewalks.

parameters.name: Crossings over bike facilities
parameters.relationship: A driveway or loading crossing over a painted or protected bike lane adds cyclist conflict, treated with green markings in the EDM; lane access removes it. Counted apart from pedestrian conflict.

parameters.name: Weather protection depth, height and continuity
parameters.relationship: Deeper, continuous canopies at 3.0-4.5 m height give longer rain-sheltered walking and waiting, but can block daylight and sky view and conflict with street trees.

parameters.name: Ground-storey floor-to-floor height
parameters.relationship: 4.6-6.1 m storeys give flexible, tall shopfront bands and mezzanines; higher ground storeys raise podium height and construction cost.

parameters.name: Street type and policy area
parameters.relationship: Street type sets how strict the active-frontage target is: continuous on the retail high street, mixed on the arterial, service tolerated on lanes. The Granville Street Plan area adds its own presets (24/7, queuing, venue entrances, screen dimming).

metrics.name: Entrance spacing on fine-grain active facades
metrics.good: About 8-12 m between entrances (roughly 8-13 per 100 m).
metrics.bad: Gaps above 12 m flagged amber; 'typically' makes it discretionary, not pass/fail. Major active uses reported apart.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S3.1.1a (Appendix A, approved 28 Jul 2026; final text not posted). Per-100 m conversion [DERIVED]; fine-grain scope from glossary.
metrics.method: Order entrance points along each street edge; report median gap, maximum gap and entrances per 100 m.

metrics.name: Fine-grain unit frontage width
metrics.good: Fine-grain active units generally 7.6-15.3 m wide.
metrics.bad: Fine-grain units wider than 15.3 m not designed to be demisable; major anchors better below or above grade.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S2.7.2 and G2.7.2 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Measure distance between demising lines or tagged unit boundaries along the facade.

metrics.name: Active frontage share by street type
metrics.good: Retail high street at least 90%; arterial and other streets at least 70%; lanes no minimum (editable presets).
metrics.bad: Below 50% on a retail high street or arterial.
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] CDDG G2.6.1 only says to locate active uses on fronting streets, corners, open spaces and links; no percentage. ODP retail-continuity map not opened.
metrics.method: Length of active segments over total street-facing frontage length, per street type.

metrics.name: Active-use depth
metrics.good: Active space at least 9.1 m deep from facade to first core or back-of-house line (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Shallower than the preset, or shelving, signage or back-of-house blocking views in (G3.1.3).
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] CDDG G2.10.2c gives 9.1 m only for frontage of above-grade parking structures; used as an analogue. G3.1.3 asks layouts to keep views in.
metrics.method: Perpendicular depth from facade to first core, back-of-house or opaque line, per active segment.

metrics.name: Lobby and entry classification
metrics.good: Hotel lobbies and transit entrances active; office and residential lobbies semi-active unless lined with retail or amenity; separate entries for residential and other uses (G2.11.1).
metrics.bad: A lobby counted active with no use on its frontage, or one shared entry for residential and other uses.
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] Glossary lists hotel lobbies and transit entrances as active (verified text); semi-active default for office and residential lobbies is ours.
metrics.method: Read lobby tag, frontage use and entry count per use; reclassify segments before totals.

metrics.name: Night-time activation and lighting
metrics.good: Reported only: share of active frontage with evening hours and integrated lighting; Granville Street Plan area also reports against its 24/7 destination principle. No sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level; long blank or dark runs and grilles impermeable at night flagged.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT, qualitative] [CORRECTED r2] CDDG G3.1.1a-c (sightlines, integrated lighting, permeable grilles at all hours), G2.16.1-2 (lighting, glare, spill); Granville Street Plan framework text now read (P06-S42). No hours rule exists.
metrics.method: Divide length with evening hours and lighting flag by active frontage length; flag dark runs; check sightlines from sidewalk into active units.

metrics.name: Granville Street Plan area chips
metrics.good: When selected: large legible venue entrances (GL1.2.2); patios and cultural spaces visible from the street (GL2.1.1); entertainment above or below the ground floor (GL2.1.2); screens dimmed after 22:00 near homes.
metrics.bad: Chip unmet without an evidence note.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT, qualitative] RTS 18459 Appendix C pp.38-39 (Granville Street Plan Urban Design Framework); plan guidelines, no numbers.
metrics.method: Show chips only for the chosen policy area; each takes a yes/no and an evidence note.

metrics.name: Ground-floor transparency ratio
metrics.good: At least 60% glazed in the band from grade to the lower of second-floor underside or canopy soffit (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Below 40% (editable preset).
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] CDDG S3.1.1b requires transparent glazing across 'most' of the ground floor, no number. Bird Friendly Design (CDDG 4.8) may cut effective transparency.
metrics.method: Glazed area over facade area in the band, from modelled openings or annotated ratio.

metrics.name: Longest blank or opaque run
metrics.good: No run longer than about 10 m (about one entrance spacing, editable).
metrics.bad: Run longer than 15 m (editable).
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] CDDG G3.1.2 and G2.15.3 say to limit blank walls, grilles, secondary egress doors and opaque glazing along streets, with no length.
metrics.method: Maximum consecutive length of blank, service or passive segments; impermeable grilles and gates count blank.

metrics.name: Weather-protection geometry
metrics.good: Mounting height 3.0-4.5 m; depth-to-height ratio about 0.4-0.7; depth at least 1.5 m in most mixed-use contexts.
metrics.bad: Outside these ranges, or missing over active frontages, transit and entries.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S3.2.1 and S3.2.2 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Sample canopy depth and underside height every 2 m along active frontage; compute ratio.

metrics.name: Weather-protection coverage of active frontage
metrics.good: Generally continuous along non-residential active frontages, at least 90% of length (preset).
metrics.bad: Below 50% of length (preset).
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] CDDG G3.2.1 asks generally continuous protection where pedestrian activity is high; percentages are placeholders.
metrics.method: Canopy length over active frontage length.

metrics.name: Vehicle access and service frontage on streets
metrics.good: Vehicle access from the lane; no driveway or loading door on retail high street or arterial frontage where lane access exists.
metrics.bad: Any street-side crossing where lane access is feasible; count and width reported.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG G2.10.1 (access from lane) and Transportation 2040 W 1.1.6 (minimise driveways across sidewalks). No numeric cap.
metrics.method: Count vehicle crossings and sum service-door lengths per street edge.

metrics.name: Crossings over bike facilities
metrics.good: No driveway or loading crossing over a bike facility where lane access exists; any crossing counted and flagged for conflict treatment.
metrics.bad: Any such crossing with feasible lane access.
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] Extension of CDDG G2.10.1. EDM 2026 Table 8-18 lists major driveway crossings of bike lanes for green treatment: context, not a limit.
metrics.method: Count crossings on edges with bike_facility painted or protected; report width and kind.

metrics.name: Active-storey floor-to-floor height
metrics.good: 4.6-6.1 m for active-use storeys.
metrics.bad: Below 4.6 m for retail, or above 6.1 m without a mezzanine rationale.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S2.7.1 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Read storey heights of tagged active volumes.

modules.method: 1) Offset each ground-storey edge facing a street, mid-block link or plaza; split at entrances, demising lines and tag changes. 2) Classify segments active, semi-active, passive, blank or service from tags, glazing, entrances, lobby class and hours (hotel lobbies and transit entrances active; office and residential lobbies semi-active, preset). 3) Tag active segments fine-grain or major; apply spacing and unit-width checks to fine-grain only. 4) Sum lengths by street type; entrances per 100 m, gaps, longest blank run. 5) Measure active depth to the first core or back-of-house line. 6) Glazing ratio from grade to lower of second-floor underside and canopy soffit. 7) Sample canopy height and depth every 2 m. 8) Count vehicle crossings, separately over bike facilities. 9) Thresholds from a JSON table with source id and status; badges at entrances and transit plaza read 'not assessed: wind' until CLIM supplies a result.
visualization: Plan view: each street edge offset 1 m outward and drawn as a thick polyline coloured by category (active green, semi-active teal, passive amber, blank grey with hatch, service purple), entrances as triangles, 10 m ticks, driveways over bike lanes marked; colour-blind-safe palette plus pattern fills.
Unrolled elevation strip per street (x = length in m, y = grade to second floor) with glazing percentage as a filled line and unit-width bars against the 7.6-15.3 m band.

Bar chart of active percentage per street with preset target line; depth as a hatch band behind each segment; one badge per clause linking to the CDDG clause and source id; grey 'not assessed: wind' badge where CLIM data is missing.
Team-assumption metrics drawn with dashed outline and an editable-threshold chip; any later-disproved threshold in the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour.
modules.human_judgment: Whether a use is genuinely active (tenant, hours, display), perceived safety and edge character, material quality at touch distance, lighting quality at night, and whether a justified breach, such as a civic anchor with a long frontage, beats the rule. The jury may reward justified breaches.
modules.limits: Layer 0 holds no openings, so glazing, depth and entrances need annotation. Activity is inferred from tags, not occupancy. VTC retail-continuity streets and character area are unknown (hypothetical site). CDDG figures are guidelines ('typically'), not by-law limits. DD character area descriptions not opened.

modules.name: Streetwall, podium setbacks and street enclosure
modules.design_question: Do podium height, tower step-back, tower separation, slenderness and floorplate give a street room of comfortable proportion, keep sky and light at the pedestrian level, and read well from eye height?
modules.effort: About 6-8 person-days in full, +1.5 for eye-level view and deterministic sky patches. 13 Nov slice (about 3): Table 2.2b band with S2.2.8 chip, Table 1.5 pairs, floorplate and S2.3.2 flags. Continuity, sky, eye-level views by 10 Dec.
inputs: Layer0.Massing: per-storey footprints and storey heights, with podium/tower split derived from first step-back
Layer0.Towers: each tower's storeys and use portions (employment, hotel, residential); development type derived: exclusively residential | mixed-use | non-residential
SiteContext.StreetEdges with right-of-way (ROW) width between building lines, including sidewalks
SiteContext.Buildings and tower sites: existing, approved and potential neighbouring towers, property lines (SITE)
SiteContext.PolicyArea: Downtown character area or Granville Street Plan area chosen by the user (CDDG 4.18)
SiteContext.NorthAngle: rotation of true north relative to the street grid
SiteContext.ViewCones: Council-approved protected view cone surfaces (CDDG 4.10; SITE)
P06-M03 EnhancedOpenSpace polygons (for the S2.2.8b chip)
outputs: StreetSections: {street_id, station_m, podium_h_m, row_w_m, hw_ratio, step_back_m, sky_view_factor}[]
PodiumBandCheck: {street_id, rule: 2.2.6 (Table 2.2b) | 2.2.7 | 2.2.8, allowed_min_m, allowed_max_m, actual_m, status}
TowerChecks: {pair_type: own-own | own-neighbour | own-property-line, use_pair, separation_m, required_m, status}[]
FloorplateAndSlenderness: {tower_id, floorplate_avg_m2, max_dimension_m, s2_3_2_flag, width_share_of_frontage, height_to_width}[]
StreetwallContinuityPct per street edge
SkyPlots: stereographic sky maps at sampled eye points (consumed by CLIM and P06-M08)
EyeLevelView: {point_id, band, sky_pct, podium_pct, tower_pct, context_pct, tree_pct}[] (reported only)
ViewConeStatus: inside | outside per tower (context flag)

parameters.name: Podium (streetwall) height
parameters.relationship: Taller podium on a given street gives a higher height-to-width ratio, stronger enclosure and less visible sky at the sidewalk (geometry). The CDDG caps podium height by street width so enclosure stays in a band.

parameters.name: Street right-of-way width (building line to building line)
parameters.relationship: Wider street (sidewalks included) allows a taller podium for the same enclosure: Table 2.2b steps from 15.2 m (up to 27.5 m wide) to 15.2-18.3 m (up to 30.5 m) and 18.3-23.0 m above 30.5 m in Downtown and the Broadway Plan Area.

parameters.name: Podium rule by development type, and exception path
parameters.relationship: Table 2.2b (S2.2.6) governs mixed-use and non-residential tower podiums; S2.2.7 (18.3 m Downtown) only exclusively residential ones. S2.2.8b lifts maxima below 21.3 m to 21.3 m on frontage over 60.7 m with enhanced open space: less sky, more ground.

parameters.name: Tower step-back above podium
parameters.relationship: A setback above the podium makes the base read as the street wall and hides tower mass from the sidewalk; the CDDG tip says a planar change of 1.5-3.0 m is the least that reads as a volumetric break.

parameters.name: Massing variation interval along the street
parameters.relationship: Variation every 25-46 m breaks long monolithic walls into a human-scale rhythm; longer unbroken runs read as monolithic.

parameters.name: Tower floorplate area and dimension
parameters.relationship: Larger floorplate gives a wider tower, wider shadow and less sky from the street (geometry). CDDG gives average maxima by use; over 29.0 m wide needs clear articulation in mixed-use contexts (S2.3.2).

parameters.name: Tower width as share of frontage
parameters.relationship: A wider face against the site frontage reads as a slab and blocks more sky; the CDDG tip says towers wider than roughly 60% of frontage often read as slabs (47.5 m of 79.2 m; 86.9 m of 144.8 m).

parameters.name: Tower slenderness
parameters.relationship: Taller, narrower towers read slender and let more sky and sun through; the CDDG tip says height-to-width of 6:1 to 8:1 or more reads proportionate for tall and very tall towers.

parameters.name: Tower separation by use pair
parameters.relationship: More separation gives more daylight, privacy and sky reaching the public realm. Table 1.5 sets 15.2-24.4 m by use pair; G1.5.1 asks for more where towers exceed typical heights, as 244-305 m towers do.

parameters.name: Intra-site tower spacing and future neighbours
parameters.relationship: Several towers on one block must each meet Table 1.5 against each other; separation is shared equally with a neighbouring tower site (S1.5.1), so a future neighbour needs half the value to the property line.

parameters.name: Corner setbacks at north-south street corners
parameters.relationship: Setting massing back at north-south corners opens street-end mountain views; the downtown grid is rotated, so 'north-south' comes from the street grid, not true north.

parameters.name: Massing over open space
parameters.relationship: Overhead massing over a POPS is not supported and cuts sun and sky; elsewhere a clear height of 12.0-18.0 m is expected under overhanging mass (S2.2.9).

parameters.name: Eye-level view composition
parameters.relationship: A larger share of sky and a smaller share of tower wall in the view at walking height should feel more open and less enclosed; direction only (street-view studies link walls and buildings to higher, sky and trees to lower perceived stress), no transferable threshold.

metrics.name: Podium height versus street width (Table 2.2b)
metrics.good: Downtown and Broadway Plan Area by ROW: up to 27.5 m wide, up to 15.2 m; up to 30.5 m, 15.2-18.3 m; over 30.5 m, 18.3-23.0 m. Other contexts up to 15.2 m. S2.2.7 (18.3 m) only for exclusively residential towers.
metrics.bad: Podium above the band for its ROW; needs a written justification.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] [CORRECTED r1, r2] CDDG Table 2.2b, S2.2.6-S2.2.8; table checked in the PDF render (r2). Glossary: 'residential development' means exclusively residential, so no 18.3 m cap on mixed-use or non-residential towers.
metrics.method: Look up ROW width; compare podium height from the first step-back with the Table 2.2b band. Choose the rule from tower uses: exclusively residential, S2.2.7; otherwise S2.2.6.

metrics.name: Podium exception for long frontage (S2.2.8b)
metrics.good: Where Table 2.2b gives under 21.3 m (ROW up to 30.5 m): up to 21.3 m if frontage exceeds 60.7 m and eligible enhanced open space exists (VTC qualifies on frontage). Over 30.5 m, 23.0 m already applies.
metrics.bad: Above the raised maximum, or 21.3 m without eligible enhanced open space.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] [CORRECTED r2] S2.2.8 raises S2.2.6 maxima; no increase over 23.0 m is our reading [DERIVED]. Glossary: enhanced open space is at grade, free of overhead buildings; S3.9.1 asks 50% planted with trees; G3.9.5 bars vehicles.
metrics.method: Test frontage over 60.7 m; test tagged enhanced open space for at grade, no overhead mass, no vehicles; show planted share from M03; compare podium with the raised maximum.

metrics.name: Implied podium height-to-width ratio
metrics.good: About 0.55-0.75 for tower podiums at each band's upper width (15.2/27.5, 18.3/30.5, 23.0/30.5); about 1:1 to 1:1.1 for low-rise residential streetwalls (S2.2.2).
metrics.bad: Above the band for the street type.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] Our arithmetic from Table 2.2b, not a quoted rule. The low-rise ratio is quoted from S2.2.2.
metrics.method: Podium height over face-to-face ROW width, sampled every 5 m along the street.

metrics.name: Tower step-back above podium
metrics.good: A massing setback above the podium (G2.2.2), with about 1.5-3.0 m planar change to read as a volumetric break.
metrics.bad: Tower faces flush with the podium plane on a street where a defined streetwall is wanted.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] G2.2.2 is a guideline with no number; 1.5-3.0 m is a CDDG design tip, not a step-back standard.
metrics.method: Horizontal offset between podium face and first tower storey face.

metrics.name: Average tower floorplate
metrics.good: Employment and hotel towers about 930-1,395 m2; residential baseline 511-670 m2; tall residential up to 746 m2; very tall residential 930-1,115 m2.
metrics.bad: Above the maximum; reviewed case by case.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG Table 2.3 and S2.3.3. Tall about 90 m, very tall about 150 m (glossary). Splitting a stacked tower's floorplate by use portion is our interpretation.
metrics.method: Slice the mesh at every tower storey; average gross floor area by use portion.

metrics.name: Tower dimension and articulation (S2.3.2)
metrics.good: Tower plan dimension at most 29.0 m, or clear volumetric articulation shown in mixed-use and non-residential contexts; slender proportions (G2.3.2).
metrics.bad: Dimension over 29.0 m with no articulation.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S2.3.1 (29.0 m limit, predominantly residential), S2.3.2 (articulation if over 29.0 m, mixed-use and non-residential), G2.3.2. Read in r2.
metrics.method: Maximum plan dimension of each tower storey slice; flag over 29.0 m and ask for an articulation note.

metrics.name: Tower width as share of frontage
metrics.good: Reported only: tower face width over site frontage; the CDDG tip flags about 60% (47.5 m on the 79.2 m side, 86.9 m on the 144.8 m side).
metrics.bad: Wider than about 60% flagged as slab-like, not failed.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] CDDG design tip (rule of thumb for a typical east-west site), not a standard; the 47.5 m and 86.9 m figures are our arithmetic.
metrics.method: Maximum tower width parallel to each street edge divided by that frontage length.

metrics.name: Tower separation by use pair
metrics.good: At or above Table 1.5: residential-residential 24.4; residential-hotel 24.4 (18.3 if S1.5.2 met); residential-employment 18.3; hotel-hotel, hotel-employment, employment-employment 15.2 m.
metrics.bad: Below the table value, unless S1.5.3 (CBD employment or hotel) applies with public-realm light protected; G1.5.2 allows only 0.6-1.0 m.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] [CORRECTED r1] CDDG Table 1.5 (checked in PDF render, r2), S1.5.1-S1.5.4, G1.5.1-G1.5.2 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Minimum face-to-face distance for every tower pair: own-own and own-neighbour at full value; unbuilt neighbour at half value to the property line; non-tower neighbour per S1.5.4.

metrics.name: Separation for very tall towers (G1.5.1)
metrics.good: Reported only: separation over the taller tower's height per pair; flag 'consider more' above about 150 m.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] G1.5.1 asks to consider more separation where towers exceed typical heights, no number; VTC towers are 244-305 m.
metrics.method: Divide each pair's separation by the taller tower's height; list pairs.

metrics.name: Tower slenderness indicator
metrics.good: Height-to-width about 6:1 to 8:1 or more for tall and very tall towers.
metrics.bad: Lower ratios flagged for added shaping, articulation or separation.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] CDDG design tip (rule of thumb), not a standard; tall and very tall defined in the glossary.
metrics.method: Tower height over the smaller plan dimension of the average floorplate.

metrics.name: Massing variation interval
metrics.good: Variation in massing about every 25.0-45.7 m of frontage.
metrics.bad: Unbroken facade longer than 45.7 m.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S2.2.1 (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Detect plane changes of at least 1.5 m along the street face; measure spacing.

metrics.name: Streetwall continuity
metrics.good: At least 80% of block-face length within 1 m of the build-to line on the retail high street (preset).
metrics.bad: Below 50% (preset).
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] CDDG G2.2.1 says maintain continuity where a continuous streetwall is desired, no percentage. One tolerance (1 m) now used in metric and method (r2).
metrics.method: Length of facade within 1 m of the street line at both 1.6 m and 12 m heights, over block-face length; report which height fails.

metrics.name: Sky view factor at sidewalk and street centre
metrics.good: Reported as change from the by-right or existing baseline; cosine-weighted and unweighted values side by side. No sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] No Vancouver threshold found; Ewing and Handy 2009 not opened. 500 random rays give a standard error of about 0.02 at 0.5 (our arithmetic); deterministic patches remove it.
metrics.method: From 1.6 m eye height, deterministic sky patches (at least 2,000, equal solid angle) with cosine weights, or an analytic view factor; also the unweighted open-sky fraction. Report both.

metrics.name: Eye-level view composition (reported only)
metrics.good: Per sidewalk point and elevation band (0-15, 15-30, 30-60, 60-90 degrees): shares of sky, podium, tower, other buildings and trees, along and across the street. No sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level; tower-dominated near-horizon views flagged for review, not failed.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] CDDG tip: test legibility, rhythm and enclosure from sidewalk viewpoints. Street-view studies (abstracts only) link walls and buildings to higher, sky and trees to lower perceived stress; no threshold. Bands are team presets.
metrics.method: Render a cube map at 1.6 m; classify each ray (sky, podium, tower, context, tree, ground); report shares per band and azimuth sector.

metrics.name: Protected view cones (context flag)
metrics.good: Reported only: tower inside or outside Council-approved view cone boundaries; CDDG 4.10 points to the Public Views Guidelines.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level here; the Public Views Guidelines were not opened.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] City memo (Apr 2026): protected public views are a fixed overlay informing where higher buildings suit, not reviewed in the Higher Buildings review.
metrics.method: Intersect tower footprints and heights with SITE view-cone surfaces; list conflicts.

modules.method: For every street edge cut perpendicular sections every 5 m. Ray-cast from a 1.6 m eye point for facing heights, face-to-face width, podium height (first step-back of at least 1.5 m) and step-back. Pick the podium rule from tower uses (Table 2.2b under S2.2.6; S2.2.7 only if exclusively residential), then test S2.2.8. Slice the mesh above the podium for floorplate, maximum dimension, slenderness and width share. Test every tower pair per Table 1.5 (own-own, own-neighbour, future neighbour at half value, S1.5.4); flag G1.5.1 above 150 m. Sky: deterministic cosine-weighted patches (at least 2,000), unweighted sky share, eye-level view shares by elevation band. Streetwall continuity within 1 m at 1.6 m and 12 m. Thresholds from versioned lookup tables with source ids.
visualization: Street cross-section drawing per frontage: podium and tower profile, eye-height cone, shaded allowed-podium band for that ROW, and the measured height-to-width ratio labelled.

Plan: each street segment coloured by podium status (inside band green, above band red, no podium grey) with tower footprints and separation lines labelled in metres against required values, intra-site pairs included.
Stereographic sky plot and eye-level panorama strip at chosen points: percentage of open sky, shares of podium and tower, baseline comparison.
Pass/fail badges linked to CDDG clause numbers; derived rows in dashed style.
modules.human_judgment: Perceived enclosure and scale in context, rhythm and proportion of the base, response to heritage or neighbours, skyline and crown quality, and any justified departure from the guideline bands.
modules.limits: CDDG tables are discretionary guidelines in draft Appendix A. Table 2.2a does not map onto the rotated grid. Sky view factor, eye-level shares and wind downwash have no sourced pass level. DD character area guides (4.18) and Public Views Guidelines not opened.

parameters.name: Public open space share of site area
parameters.relationship: More public open space (POPS, mid-block links, plazas) gives more room for gathering, trees and sun, but less building footprint. VTC block is about 11,468 m2: 20% is about 2,294 m2, a POPS of about 10% about 1,147 m2.

parameters.name: POPS shape, contiguity and size
parameters.relationship: A contiguous space of about 300 m2 or more with 1:1-1:2 proportions is usable as a neighbourhood space; narrow or fragmented leftovers do not qualify and read as private.

parameters.name: Overhead massing and podium location of the space
parameters.relationship: Mass over a POPS removes it from the POPS count and cuts sun and sky; space on podium or roof without public stairs and lifts also does not count.

parameters.name: Planted share of enhanced open space
parameters.relationship: More planted area with trees (S3.9.1 asks at least 50% of enhanced open space) gives shade, habitat and softer edges but less paved plaza for gathering; whether it applies to a non-residential tower site is unresolved.

parameters.name: Tower height, floorplate and position relative to protected spaces
parameters.relationship: Taller, wider tower south or west of a space gives a longer, wider shadow and fewer sunlit hours there. Reach is H / tan(sun elevation): about 600 m for 305 m on 22 Sep (27 degrees at 10:00), about 1.4 km on 11 Nov.

parameters.name: Test date, time window and UTC offset
parameters.relationship: Each protected space has its own date and window (22 Sep 10:00-16:00; Robson Village to 15:00; Victory Square cenotaph 11 Nov 10:00-12:00). The offset moves each instant by an hour, which changes the shadow cast.

parameters.name: Study type: Basic or Detailed
parameters.relationship: Basic (two-hour instants) is for every applicant; Detailed (15-minute, 25 instants, area take-offs, coverage %) is needed to argue an exception. Running Detailed early shows the shadow budget but costs run time.

parameters.name: Own-POPS study date and window
parameters.relationship: People use a POPS mostly at lunchtime and in late spring and summer; testing only the City window (22 Sep, 10:00-16:00) can miss when the space is actually used. Extra windows are team presets; the City may also ask other dates (3.1.4).

parameters.name: Wind exposure at grade points
parameters.relationship: Taller towers and open corners tend to raise ground wind at seating, entrances, sidewalks, transit plaza, links and terraces, giving fewer comfortable hours and, at the extreme, unsafe gusts. CDDG G1.8.1b says site open space to minimise wind exposure.

parameters.name: Wind-mitigation geometry (podium edge, canopy, step-back)
parameters.relationship: Tower setbacks, large podiums, rounded or stepped corners and canopies are wind-control measures in the Toronto guide, and tapered or setback shapes helped in one CFD study; effect size is unsourced for Vancouver and belongs to CLIM.

parameters.name: Seating quantity and type
parameters.relationship: More seating with backs, in sun and shade, at corners and links gives longer stays and wider use by older people. NYC rule: 1 linear ft per 30 sq ft, three types above 465 m2, moveable seating above 929 m2.

parameters.name: Retail patio share of a POPS
parameters.relationship: More private patio inside a POPS gives less space and less perceived publicness; CDDG limits patios to about one third of a POPS.

parameters.name: Access hours and legal tenure (SRW)
parameters.relationship: Longer, unconditional hours and a statutory right-of-way make the space work as public; early closing or gates reduce use. NYC default is open at all times, with limited closings only by authorisation.

parameters.name: Planting, soil volume and underground setbacks
parameters.relationship: Underground setbacks and slab drops enable in-ground trees, shade and habitat; CDDG asks tree planting in plazas where contiguous planted areas or setbacks exist, with soil depths per the CSLA standard (S4.5.1).

parameters.name: Transit plaza size
parameters.relationship: Space next to a station entrance sized for waiting and circulation (about 6.1 m by 6.1 m at least) supports transit use; it is not counted toward park dedication.

metrics.name: Public open space as share of site area
metrics.good: At least 20% of site area (about 2,294 m2) as public open space, counting POPS, mid-block links and plazas; vehicle space excluded.
metrics.bad: Below 20%. The 10% mid-sized-site target (S1.9.2) does not apply to an 11,468 m2 block; park dedication may be requested.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT clause; applicability to VTC = team assumption] [CORRECTED r1] CDDG S1.9.1 (large or unique sites) and glossary: large sites refer to the Rezoning Policy for Sustainable Large Developments (not opened), unique sites to the area plan.
metrics.method: Sum tagged public open space meeting counting rules; divide by 11,468 m2.

metrics.name: POPS component of the open-space total
metrics.good: POPS about 10% of site area (about 1,147 m2) on mixed-use and non-residential tower sites with frontage over 60.7 m (VTC qualifies); counts toward the 20% total.
metrics.bad: Below about 10%, fragmented or under mass.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S1.10.2 and glossary (POPS is a public open space). Whether S1.10.2 is extra to or inside the 20% is unresolved; tool counts it inside.
metrics.method: Area of eligible POPS polygons over site area.

metrics.name: POPS geometry and eligibility
metrics.good: Contiguous, proportion 1:1 or 1:2, area about 300 m2 or more, secured by SRW, free of overhead massing; excludes setbacks, engineering SRWs, vehicle space, and podium or roof areas without public stairs and lifts.
metrics.bad: Fragmented, under mass, without SRW or access points.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S1.11.1 and glossary definition of POPS.
metrics.method: Apply eligibility filters to tagged polygons; minimum bounding rectangle aspect.

metrics.name: Enhanced open space eligibility and planting
metrics.good: At grade, free of overhead buildings (balconies excluded), no vehicles, at least 50% planted with trees; modest private encroachments only (patios, up to 3 m amenity).
metrics.bad: Overhead mass, vehicle circulation, or under 50% planted where the rule applies.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT clause; applicability unresolved] Glossary, S3.9.1, G3.9.2, G3.9.5. S3.9 is titled for densifying residential neighbourhoods; use on a non-residential tower site is our reading.
metrics.method: Test polygon at grade, no overhead mass or vehicles; planted area with tree planting over area.

metrics.name: Shadow analysis domain
metrics.good: Radius at least H / tan(lowest sun elevation in the window): about 600 m for 305 m on 22 Sep (UTC-7); about 1.4 km on 11 Nov at UTC-7, 0.9 km at UTC-8.
metrics.bad: A fixed small radius that omits protected spaces within reach.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] Our NOAA-algorithm calculation at 49.28 N: elevation 26.9 degrees at 10:00 and 28.1 at 16:00 on 22 Sep; 12.6 degrees at 10:00 on 11 Nov (UTC-7). Reach 305 / tan 26.9 = 601 m.
metrics.method: R = H_max / tan(el_min) over the instants of each rule; keep Table 1 spaces within R; report R in the UI.

metrics.name: Shadow polygon construction for stepped massing
metrics.good: Per-slab projection agrees with a ray-cast check at sample points on a stepped massing (podium plus tower); mismatch reported, within the grid discretisation bound (team preset).
metrics.bad: One convex hull over podium and tower, which overstates shadow and can fail protected parks falsely.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] [CORRECTED r2] Geometry: the shadow of a constant-footprint slab is its footprint swept along the shadow direction; union of both end polygons and swept edge parallelograms is exact for non-convex plans.
metrics.method: For each slab (same footprint, base z0 to top z1) sweep the footprint from z0/tan(el) to z1/tan(el) along the shadow azimuth; union all slabs; compare with trimesh rays on one stepped test massing.

metrics.name: Direct sun on own public open space
metrics.good: At least 50% of POPS area has 2 or more hours of direct sun on 22 Sep between 10:00 and 16:00 (UTC-7) (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Less than 25% of area reaches 2 hours (editable preset).
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] Vancouver sets the window but no minimum sun for private open space. The 2-hour, 50% test follows BRE BR 209 practice (recalled, not opened), moved from 21 March to 22 Sep.
metrics.method: Test 0.5 m cell centres against unioned shadow polygons at 25 instants; hours = trapezoid sum (end weights 0.5) times 0.25 h, maximum 6.0 h. Extra windows optional.

metrics.name: New shadow: parks, school sites, Dilawri Square South, Jack Poole Plaza, Robson Square
metrics.good: No new shadow within property lines on 22 Sep, 10:00-16:00 (UTC-7).
metrics.bad: FAIL by default. Exception path 3.1.2: public benefit, shadow rationale statement, Detailed study; staff weigh 3.1.3 items.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] Solar Access Guidelines (memo RTS 16506, Appendix A) 3.1.1-3.1.3, 4.2.1 and Table 1 classes.
metrics.method: Project shadow per instant, union, intersect with the space polygon; any added area above numerical tolerance fails.

metrics.name: Exception evidence form (3.1.3 and 3.3.3)
metrics.good: Staff weigh: (a) quality and function of the space at key times, including limiting impacts to vulnerable populations; (b) shadow duration; (c) parcel constraints; (d) mitigation explored; (e) base-zoning expectations (rezonings).
metrics.bad: Exception argued without these fields, or without a Detailed study.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] Memo RTS 16506 Appendix A, 3.1.3 a-e and 3.3.3 a-e (read r2).
metrics.method: Form with one field per item a-e, completed by people; attach Detailed study outputs.

metrics.name: New shadow: Dr Sun Yat-Sen Gardens and Park
metrics.good: No new shadow at any time between 10:00 and 16:00 on 22 Sep.
metrics.bad: FAIL. Section 4.1 states no exception path; whether 3.1.2 applies is unresolved.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] Memo RTS 16506 Appendix A, 4.1.1 ('despite' 3.1) and Table 1 (Local park, refer to 4.1).
metrics.method: As for parks; Basic study at two-hour instants plus a finer check.

metrics.name: New shadow: Victory Square and Cenotaph circle
metrics.good: No new shadow in the park (3.1.1) and none on the Cenotaph circle 10:00-12:00 on 11 Nov.
metrics.bad: FAIL. Exception only after comprehensive public and key stakeholder engagement (4.3.2, which cites '4.5.1', read as 4.3.1). Run 11 Nov at UTC-8 and UTC-7 because 4.3.1 says PST.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] Memo RTS 16506 Appendix A, 4.3.1-4.3.2 and Table 1 (urban plaza, refer to 4.3). 4.3.1 applies in addition to 3.1.
metrics.method: Second solar date; shadow polygons on the Cenotaph circle for both offsets.

metrics.name: New shadow: Davie and Robson Village north sidewalks
metrics.good: No new shadow on the north sidewalk, curb to property line: Davie 10:00-16:00, Robson 10:00-15:00 on 22 Sep.
metrics.bad: FAIL by default. Exception path 3.3.2: public benefit, shadow rationale, Detailed study of affected blocks.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] Memo RTS 16506 Appendix A, 3.3.1-3.3.3, Maps 2 and 3.
metrics.method: Intersect shadow union with the sidewalk strip polygons per instant.

metrics.name: New shadow: West End miniparks and other urban plazas
metrics.good: Report added shadow and explore strategies to minimise it where possible; no pass or fail.
metrics.bad: Added shadow with no mitigation record.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] [CORRECTED r1] Memo Appendix A, 3.2.1. Jack Poole Plaza, Robson Square, Dilawri South and Victory Square are special cases.
metrics.method: Same projection; verdict 'minimise' (amber), never a hard fail.

metrics.name: Indigenous-named Table 1 spaces
metrics.good: Print official names as published. Urban Plazas šxʷƛ̓ənəq Xwtl'e7énḵ and šxʷƛ̓exən Xwtl'a7shn follow 3.2.1 (minimise); Neighbourhood park sθəqəlxenəm ts'exwts'áxwi7 (Rainbow Park) follows 3.1.1. All three go to human review.
metrics.bad: Names retyped, anglicised or dropped, or plaza shadow reported without human review.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] Memo Table 1 (read r2); former names: Vancouver Art Gallery North Plaza, Queen Elizabeth Theatre Plaza. Orthography is from the PDF text layer: import from City data and check glyph by glyph.
metrics.method: Flag rows by Table 1 name; route to the human-review queue and the M08 cultural log.

metrics.name: Study type and coverage formula
metrics.good: Basic study (10:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00) for every application; Detailed study (25 instants, area take-offs, coverage %) when an exception to 3.1.1 or 3.3.1 is argued.
metrics.bad: Detailed omitted when an exception is argued, or the 15-minute run presented as the standard test.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] [CORRECTED r1] Memo Appendix A, 5.1.1 and 5.2.1. Coverage % = total shadow area over 25 instants / (space area x 25), as the City defines it.
metrics.method: Basic: 4 instants. Detailed: 25 instants; existing, added and cumulative m2 per instant; City coverage formula.

metrics.name: Study inputs and time base
metrics.good: Model set to Pacific Time as UTC-7 with complete built and approved context, known proposed developments and topography; new shadow shown apart from existing; trees and small structures excluded from baseline.
metrics.bad: Context, proposed buildings or terrain missing, or a seasonal offset used.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] [CORRECTED r1] Memo Appendix A section 5 (PDT, UTC-7); Council report RTS 18459 App. D replaces PDT with PT. Victory Square text still says PST.
metrics.method: Fix UTC-7 in the solar routine, show the offset in the UI, include proposed and approved buildings and terrain.

metrics.name: Seating supply
metrics.good: 1 ft per 30 sq ft (about 10.9 m per 100 m2); two types, three above 465 m2; at least 50% of fixed seating with backs; moveable chairs above 929 m2; seating at corners and links.
metrics.bad: Less than half of the NYC quantity, or no seating at corners and links.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] NYC ZR 37-741: text verified, not a Vancouver rule; team preset. CDDG G3.4.2 supports seating at corners and links.
metrics.method: Sum linear seating metres by type and plaza area; count backs on fixed seating; moveable chairs at 1 per 18.6 m2.

metrics.name: Wind comfort and safety at grade points
metrics.good: Benchmark: GEM at 80% of 6:00-23:00 per season; sitting 10 km/h (seating, cafes, terraces), standing 15 km/h (entrances, bus stops), walking 20 km/h (sidewalks, lanes). Safety: gust above 90 km/h no more than 0.1% of hours.
metrics.bad: GEM over 20 km/h for 20% of time where people go; any safety exceedance is a hard flag; no CLIM result shows 'not assessed: wind', never green.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] Toronto Pedestrian Level Wind Study ToR Guide 2022, Table 3 (text read); Toronto climate, not adopted by Vancouver. CDDG G1.8.1b is qualitative. CLIM confirms or replaces.
metrics.method: GEM = max(mean, gust / 1.85); intersect CLIM grid with each point set; report class shares and exceedance hours.

metrics.name: Access hours and tenure
metrics.good: Public open space secured by SRW and open at least from 7:00 to 22:00 in summer and 7:00 to 20:00 in winter; mid-block links 24 hours (preset).
metrics.bad: Hours shorter than the NYC allowed-closing schedule, ticketed entry, or no SRW.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] CDDG requires SRWs for POPS and links but no hours; hours from NYC ZR 37-727.
metrics.method: Read access attributes; compare to the schedule.

metrics.name: Retail patio share of POPS
metrics.good: Patios no more than about one third of the POPS; signage states public use.
metrics.bad: Above one third, or no public-use signage.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S3.6.1 and S3.6.2.
metrics.method: Patio area over POPS area.

metrics.name: Transit plaza minimum size
metrics.good: At least about 6.1 m by 6.1 m beside a station entrance.
metrics.bad: Smaller, or counted toward park dedication.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S4.4.1; section 1.9 special note (transit plazas not considered for park dedication). G1.9.1 was mis-cited before r2.
metrics.method: Largest inscribed rectangle in the plaza polygon.

modules.method: 1) Tag ground-plane polygons; apply CDDG counting rules; report share of 11,468 m2. 2) Solar position (NOAA algorithm, fixed UTC offset) per rule date and window. 3) Domain R = H / tan(lowest elevation); keep Table 1 spaces within R. 4) Per instant, project each constant-footprint slab (footprint swept from base to top height along the shadow direction: both end polygons plus swept edge parallelograms), union all slabs and context, intersect each space; take-offs and City coverage %. 5) Validate on a stepped massing against trimesh ray casts; report error. 6) Own POPS: test 0.5 m cell centres against the union; trapezoid sun hours. 7) Run in the browser (Pyodide: shapely, numpy). 8) Sum seating; intersect CLIM wind grid with point sets; badges stay 'not assessed: wind' without it.
visualization: Ground-plane false-colour mesh of direct-sun hours with a 0-6 h legend, a bold contour at 2 h, POPS outlines hatched, seating points on top, and a 15-minute time scrubber from 10:00 to 16:00.

Shadow-reach disc around the site with Table 1 spaces inside it, labelled by official name, coloured by rule (no-new-shadow red when breached, minimise amber), radius labelled; Indigenous-named spaces carry a human-review marker.
Protected-space panel: stacked area chart of existing and added shadow percent against time, City coverage percentage printed; Basic and Detailed tabs; exception evidence form beside it.

Horizontal bars of public open space percent against 10% and 20% lines; pass/fail badges linked to CDDG and solar-guideline clauses; team-assumption rows dashed, external benchmarks in their own style; grey 'not assessed: wind' badges.
modules.human_judgment: Programming and stewardship, who the space feels welcome to, perceived safety, place-making with Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh, park dedication versus POPS (City and Park Board), and whether a shadow trade-off is justified by public benefit and vulnerable users (3.1.3a).
modules.limits: Sun uses clear-sky geometry; Vancouver is often overcast in fall. Trees and small structures are ignored, as in the City baseline. v1 treats each space as a flat plane. CDDG space targets are guidelines; stacking of 20% and POPS 10% is unresolved. Shadow run time with per-slab projection is not benchmarked.

modules.name: Permeability, mid-block connections and block structure
modules.design_question: Does the block give direct, legible, step-free-ready public routes through it, and does the below-grade station link work as public realm, not just as a graph edge?
modules.effort: About 6-8 person-days in full. 13 Nov slice (about 1.5): link presence and width, SRW flag, G4.4.1-G4.4.2 manual checklist form. Walk graph, directness, isochrones by 10 Dec.
inputs: SiteBoundary and SiteContext.StreetNetwork (streets, lanes, existing mid-block links) from OSM or City open data
Layer0.Massing and ground-plane passage polylines with clear width, open-to-sky flag, hours and SRW flag
SiteContext.TransitEntrances: existing station entrance and the required below-grade secondary entrance (from MOBI packet or site plan)
SiteContext.BelowGradeLink: drawn path, clear width, lifts, stairs, level changes, sightline points to grade and concourse (user or MOBI)
Destinations: retail high street, arterial crossings, parks, plazas (from SITE packet)
CLIM wind result at link ends and transit plaza (optional; absent = 'not assessed: wind')

ConnectionChecks: {connection_id, required, clear_width_m, min_required_m, status}[]
LinkQualityChecks: Check[] for the below-grade link (G4.4.2 items) and the G4.4.1 a-h checklist, with wind_state
DirectnessTable: {from, to, network_m, straight_m, prd}[] (PRD = pedestrian route directness)
Isochrones: polygons for 2-, 5- and 10-minute walks from the station entrance
RouteGraph for P06-M05 (flows) and P06-M06 (step-free routing)

parameters.name: Number and location of mid-block connections
parameters.relationship: More public through-routes give shorter walks, more route choice and more active edges; each link removes buildable area. CDDG requires one where the site is adjacent to or includes a station entrance.

parameters.name: Connection width (building face to building face)
parameters.relationship: Wider links feel safer and allow daylight and active edges but cost site area. For the VTC block S1.12.2c sets 9.1 m face to face; 2.4 m clear path (S3.8.1). 4.5, 5.4 and 7.3 m apply to other cases.

parameters.name: Open to sky versus covered breezeway
parameters.relationship: Covered links need height-to-width of at least 2:1, active edges, a direct line and public hours or they read as tunnels; open-to-sky links are the default.

parameters.name: Alignment with desire lines and destinations
parameters.relationship: Links that join the station, parks and high street pick up existing pedestrian flows; links to nowhere stay empty and unsafe.

parameters.name: Route directness (network over straight-line distance)
parameters.relationship: Detours above straight-line distance raise walking time and reduce use; connected street networks are positively associated with physical activity in a meta-analysis (mainly children).

parameters.name: Hours of public access of each link
parameters.relationship: Links closed outside building hours cut the network at night; breezeways may be limited to building hours by the CDDG, mid-block links secured by SRW are public.

parameters.name: Grade separation of the transit link
parameters.relationship: A below-grade secondary entrance takes crowds off the surface but needs lifts, stairs, active uses and a visual link to the concourse to stay legible.

parameters.name: Lifts, stairs and level changes on the below-grade link
parameters.relationship: More than one lift keeps the link step-free when one fails; fewer level changes shorten the trip. CDDG G4.4.2b asks at least an elevator and a staircase.

parameters.name: Active edges and sightlines along the link
parameters.relationship: Active uses lining the link, with views to grade and the concourse, make it legible and safer; a blank tunnel deters use (G4.4.2c-d).

parameters.name: Station-entrance form and plaza fit-out
parameters.relationship: G4.4.2a pulls the overbuild and plaza fit-out guidelines (G4.4.1: continuous streetwall with plaza space, complementary paving, seating, shade, weather protection, integrated station equipment) onto any integrated entrance, shaping the block's ground plane.

metrics.name: Mid-block connection required by station adjacency
metrics.good: At least one public connection provided where the site includes or adjoins a station entrance.
metrics.bad: No connection although the trigger applies.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S1.12.1b and G1.12.2 (draft Appendix A). The VTC brief requires a secondary transit entrance, so the trigger applies.
metrics.method: Check presence and endpoints of connections against station entrance location.

metrics.name: Connection width
metrics.good: VTC preset: at least 9.1 m building face to building face (station-adjacent large site) with a 2.4 m clear path.
metrics.bad: Narrower: show a 'G1.12.1 variation, justify' chip, not a pass. Context rows only: 4.5 m face to line when the neighbour delivers half; 5.4 m non-residential; 7.3 m voluntary.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] [CORRECTED r1] CDDG S1.12.2c (large sites or sites identified in S1.12.1), S3.8.1 clear path; variations by G1.12.1.
metrics.method: Minimum distance between facing facades along the link centreline.

metrics.name: Open to sky or compliant breezeway
metrics.good: Primarily open to sky; a breezeway only if height-to-width at least 2:1, lined with active uses, direct and public, open during building hours.
metrics.bad: Enclosed passage not meeting these tests.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S1.12.4 and S2.2.10.
metrics.method: Compute roofed share and height-to-width of each link.

metrics.name: Below-grade link: elevator and staircase
metrics.good: At least one elevator and one staircase on each integrated station entrance.
metrics.bad: Stair only or lift only.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG G4.4.2b (applies where a development includes integrated station entrances).
metrics.method: Count tagged lifts and stairs on the link graph.

metrics.name: Below-grade link: lift redundancy
metrics.good: At least two lifts on the link so one outage does not break step-free access (editable preset).
metrics.bad: A single lift.
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] CDDG asks only 'an elevator'; redundancy pending TransLink input (MOBI).
metrics.method: Count lifts serving the same level change.

metrics.name: Below-grade link: active uses and visual connection
metrics.good: Active uses next to the secondary entrance and on the concourse level; strong visual connection to the concourse and below-grade active uses; consider washrooms.
metrics.bad: Blank link, or no sightline between grade and concourse.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG G4.4.2c-e (draft Appendix A).
metrics.method: Share of link edge tagged active; ray test from grade entrance to concourse points.

metrics.name: Integrated station entrance checklist (G4.4.2a pulls in G4.4.1)
metrics.good: G4.4.1 a-h with evidence note each: full-footprint overbuild where feasible; continuous streetwall with plaza space; complementary facade, paving; seating, cycling, shade, weather protection; integrated equipment; multiple doors; staff parking where possible.
metrics.bad: Items missing without a reason; checklist skipped.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] [CORRECTED r2] G4.4.2a: integrated entrances meet the overbuild and plaza fit-out guidelines of 4.4.1; the VTC secondary entrance triggers it. G1.8.5 asks a transit plaza.
metrics.method: Manual checklist with an evidence note per item; overbuild-dependent items marked 'where feasible'.

metrics.name: Route directness between key pairs
metrics.good: At most 1.25 for station to high street, and across-block pairs (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Above 1.5 (editable preset).
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] No sourced Vancouver or other threshold opened. Transportation 2040 notes the grid gives direct walking routes.
metrics.method: Shortest path length on the walk graph over straight-line distance.

metrics.name: Longest stretch of block perimeter without a public through-route
metrics.good: At most about 100 m (editable preset); the VTC long side is 144.8 m, so one link near the middle gives about 72 m.
metrics.bad: Above 150 m (editable preset).
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] No sourced block-length rule found for Vancouver; starting value.
metrics.method: Distance between consecutive public openings along the block perimeter.

metrics.name: Public access tenure of required links
metrics.good: Required links secured by SRW and open to the public.
metrics.bad: No SRW or access limited to a private operator's hours.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG S1.12.3 asks an SRW; 24-hour opening is not stated.
metrics.method: Read SRW flag and hours attribute.

metrics.name: Below-grade link width and daylight
metrics.good: Reported only: clear width and daylight or sky view at grade openings; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] CDDG gives no width or daylight value for station links; TransLink standards not opened (MOBI packet).
metrics.method: Minimum clear width along the drawn link; count of openings to grade.

metrics.name: Street intersection density (context scale)
metrics.good: Reported only; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Intersection density is positively associated with physical activity in a systematic review (mainly children); LEED ND thresholds not opened.
metrics.method: OSMnx intersections within 800 m of the site over area.

modules.method: Build a walk graph from streets, lanes, sidewalks, mid-block links, passages and the below-grade link; each edge carries length, clear width, open-to-sky flag and hours. Check each connection against 9.1 m (VTC) and sky-openness. Shortest paths between station entrances, high-street midpoint, crossings and M01 entrances; directness = network over straight distance. 2-, 5- and 10-minute walk areas at a preset speed. Longest perimeter stretch without a public through-route. Score the below-grade link against G4.4.2 and run the G4.4.1 a-h checklist (triggered by G4.4.2a) as manual evidence. Link-end and plaza badges read 'not assessed: wind' until CLIM supplies a result. Optional: intersection density, space syntax.
visualization: Plan with the walk graph drawn over the block: edges coloured by clear width (below 2.4 m red, 2.4-9.1 m amber, 9.1 m and over green for links), open-to-sky edges solid and covered edges dashed.
Isochrone rings (2, 5, 10 minutes) from the station entrance, shaded by time, with labelled route directness for the three key pairs.
Section strip of the below-grade link: lifts, stairs, active edge share, sightline to grade and concourse drawn and checked; G4.4.1 a-h checklist beside it.
Perimeter ruler around the block marking public openings and the longest gap; pass/fail badges linked to CDDG clauses; team-assumption rows editable; grey 'not assessed: wind' badges.
modules.human_judgment: Legibility and sightlines, whether the link feels public rather than private, night-time safety, wayfinding including Indigenous place names, and negotiation with TransLink and the neighbouring site for the secondary station entrance.
modules.limits: Pure geometry: no crowding, weather or pedestrian choice. Route directness and block-gap thresholds are presets without a source. Walking speed is a preset. The below-grade link must be drawn by the user; Layer 0 may not include it. G4.4.1 is a manual checklist.

modules.name: Sidewalk capacity and pedestrian level of service
modules.design_question: At peak times and in short surges, are sidewalks, crossings and corners around the block wide enough for comfortable walking once furniture, queues and station flows are counted?
modules.effort: About 5-7 person-days for static footway and crossing comfort with sensitivity bands; agent-based simulation (roadmap) adds 8-10. Not in the 13 Nov slice; ships by 10 Dec.
inputs: StreetSections: sidewalk total width, building edge, trees, furniture, bike racks, canopy posts (SITE and user sections)
P06-M01 Entrances and program GFA by use from Layer 0
MOBI: station and bus-stop flows (persons per peak hour and peak 15 minutes) at the transit entrances
P06-M07 PublicLiftQueue: queue persons and area at the street-level public lift lobby
PedestrianDemandPreset: person trips per 100 m2 GFA by use, peak-hour share, walk share, low/central/high multipliers (editable team assumptions)
Street area type: high street | office and retail | residential | tourist attraction | transport interchange; crossing signal timings
outputs: FootwayComfort: {segment_id, flow_pph, flow_peak15_pph, ppmm, pcl_class, area_type_verdict (peak and average-of-maximum), clear_width_m, required_width_m}[]
WidthBudget: stacked widths building buffer + active zone + clear + furniture + kerb buffer
CrossingComfort: {crossing_id, arm_pcl, island_rows}[]
CornerQueueAreas: polygons with area per person
PCLChecks: Check[] (consumed by P06-M08)

parameters.name: Peak-hour and peak 15-minute pedestrian flow
parameters.relationship: More office, retail and hotel floor area, and closer transit, give higher peak flows on adjacent sidewalks; end-of-day egress and train surges exceed the hourly mean. Rates per m2 are team assumptions.

parameters.name: Effective clear width
parameters.relationship: Total width minus 0.2 m building and kerb buffers and furniture buffers; flow per metre rises as obstacles are added, and one bench or tree pit can drop comfort a class.

parameters.name: Flow per metre of width (ppmm)
parameters.relationship: Pedestrians per minute per metre of effective width (people per hour / 60 / clear width): higher values mean more bumping and slower walking, from under 3 ppmm (A+) to over 35 ppmm (E).

parameters.name: Area type and tolerance
parameters.relationship: High streets and tourist attractions tolerate least crowding, with the same guidance for peak and average-of-maximum; residential is intermediate; office/retail and interchange tolerate most. B+ is recommended everywhere.

parameters.name: Static activity (queues, window shoppers, cafe seating)
parameters.relationship: People standing or sitting use width that walkers cannot; patios and displays can reduce clearway below 2.4 m if not allowed for. Granville Street Plan area asks queuing areas and resting spots.

parameters.name: Building setback or SRW widening
parameters.relationship: Setting the building back adds clear width at no street cost; commercial corridors have been asked for at least 5.5 m from back of curb (1.0 m back boulevard, 3.0 m clear, 1.5 m front boulevard).

parameters.name: Transit arrival surges
parameters.relationship: Train arrivals deliver short, high peaks at station entrances; check peak 15 minutes and, for interchange segments, TfL's average-of-maximum level (busiest 10-second samples) rather than the hourly mean.

parameters.name: Crossing time and corner waiting
parameters.relationship: Shorter signal time available to cross raises relative flow on the crossing arm; wider corners and islands give waiting people more space. TfL: more than three queue rows on an island pushed people to cross outside it.

parameters.name: Demand sensitivity band
parameters.relationship: Low, central and high demand multipliers show which width decision holds across plausible rates; a design that fails only in the high case is a judgment call, not a fault.

metrics.name: Pedestrian Comfort Level by area type
metrics.good: B+ (9-11 ppmm) recommended everywhere. Peak acceptable to: high street and tourist B; residential B-; office/retail and interchange C+.
metrics.bad: Peak at risk: B-, C+, C-; unacceptable from C+, C-, D. Average-of-maximum: residential at risk C+ to C-, unacceptable D; office/retail and interchange at risk C- to D, unacceptable E. Never below C+ at peak even with compensation.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK, text verified] [CORRECTED r1, r2] TfL Pedestrian Comfort Guidance 2010, Fig 8-9 and p.12 compensation note; Figure 9 decoded in r2 from its vector fills and checked against the column notes.
metrics.method: ppmm = pph / 60 / clear width; map to the PCL table and the area-type row (peak and average-of-maximum columns).

metrics.name: Peak-hour and peak 15-minute check
metrics.good: Both peak hour and peak 15 minutes meet the area-type floor; average-of-maximum checked where measured data exists.
metrics.bad: Fails only in the 15-minute surge: widen or add queue space.
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] Hourly means hide surges. TfL's average of maximum comes from busiest 10-second samples inside its spreadsheet; no hourly conversion published, so the 15-minute proxy is ours.
metrics.method: Run the PCL calculation for the peak hour, the busiest 15 minutes and the low, central and high multipliers.

metrics.name: Clear sidewalk width, Vancouver standard
metrics.good: Commercial and mixed-use streets: at least 3.0 m clear, wider by volume; downtown clearways of 3.0-5.0 m exist; 4.0 m for new high-volume corridors.
metrics.bad: Below 2.4 m (the constrained minimum) or below 3.0 m on commercial streets without City Engineer agreement.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] Engineering Design Manual 2026, Section 8.4.3.1 and Table 8-3.
metrics.method: Read clear width from the section after removing furniture and patio encroachment.

metrics.name: Pedestrian realm depth from back of curb
metrics.good: About 5.5 m (1.0 m back boulevard + 3.0 m clear + 1.5 m front boulevard) on commercial corridors.
metrics.bad: Below that without a City Engineer-approved reason.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] EDM 2026, Section 8.4.3.1 (historic request for redevelopment projects).
metrics.method: Measure back of curb to property line plus SRW.

metrics.name: Recommended total footway width by flow class
metrics.good: Under 600 pph: 2.9 m; 600-1,200: 4.2 m; 1,200-2,000: 5.3 m (3.3 m without furniture). Above 2,000 pph derive clear width = pph / 60 / 11 (B+ ceiling), plus 0.2 m buffers and furniture.
metrics.bad: Below the recommended width; above 2,000 pph the table no longer applies.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK, text verified] [CORRECTED r1] TfL Appendix B (comfortable up to 2,000 pph); the above-2,000 rule is [DERIVED] from the B+ band.
metrics.method: Classify segment flow; compare total width, or compute required clear width from ppmm.

metrics.name: Crossing arm and island comfort
metrics.good: Crossing arm better than C-; island queue at most three rows; relative pph = pph / share of time available to cross.
metrics.bad: Arm at C-, D or E (TfL mitigation trigger), or more than three queue rows.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] TfL crossing method (Step 2): text verified, London signals, not adopted locally.
metrics.method: Relative pph and ppmm on each arm and island from signal timings; count queue rows.

metrics.name: Corner queue area per person
metrics.good: Reported only: area per waiting person at corners and the transit entrance; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: No sourced fail level.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Fruin queueing densities not opened; TfL gives crossing island rows only.
metrics.method: Corner polygon area minus furniture, over peak waiting persons.

metrics.name: Footway minimum and obstacle gaps
metrics.good: Footway at least 2.0 m (1.5 m acceptable under constraint); gaps at obstacles at least 1.0 m and no longer than 6 m.
metrics.bad: Below these.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] UK DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.2; text verified, not adopted by Vancouver.
metrics.method: Scan sections for obstacle gaps.

metrics.name: Street-furniture placement
metrics.good: Furniture set back to keep sightlines at driveways, crosswalks and intersections (typically 10 m from intersections); not blocking station or emergency egress.
metrics.bad: Furniture blocking sightlines at a driveway or crossing.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] EDM 2026 Chapter 9, p.341; the earlier '1.0 m from crossings and entrances' was not found in 8.4.3, 8.4.9 or Chapter 9.
metrics.method: Check furniture points against driveway, crosswalk and intersection points.

metrics.name: Legacy Fruin level of service cross-check
metrics.good: Level C or better by area per pedestrian (values to be confirmed).
metrics.bad: Level E or F.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Fruin 1971 and HCM thresholds recalled, not opened. TfL says Fruin only assesses crowding, not comfort.
metrics.method: Area per pedestrian from density; map to Fruin classes.

metrics.name: Peak pedestrian generation assumptions
metrics.good: Editable presets by use with low, central and high multipliers, flagged as assumptions.
metrics.bad: Any figure without a source or label.
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] No sourced Vancouver trip generation rates found. Transportation 2040 target (two-thirds of trips on foot, bike or transit by 2040) is context only.
metrics.method: GFA by use times rate times peak-hour share times walk share, times multiplier.

modules.method: For each sidewalk segment adjacent to the site build the width budget: total width minus 0.2 m building buffer, 0.2 m kerb buffer and buffers around trees, poles, benches, racks and canopy posts (TfL method). Distribute person-trips from each entrance (P06-M01), public-lift queues (P06-M07) and station flows (MOBI) onto segments by shortest paths on the P06-M04 walk graph, for peak hour and peak 15 minutes, at low, central and high multipliers. Convert flow to ppmm and map to the PCL class for the area type (Figure 9, peak and average-of-maximum). Report required width for B+ and the shortfall; above 2,000 pph compute width from ppmm. Run crossing-arm and island checks from signal timings. Check Vancouver clear-width and realm-depth standards. Optionally run agent-based simulation.
visualization: Plan view: each sidewalk segment drawn as a ribbon coloured by PCL class (11-class scale from A+ blue to E dark red) with a ppmm legend and the area-type floor marked.
Cross-section bars per segment: building buffer, active zone, clear width, furniture, kerb buffer, with a marker at the width needed for B+.
Line chart of ppmm against hour of day with a low-central-high band, the B+ line and the area-type floor line drawn.
Pass/fail badges linked to TfL and EDM clauses; external-benchmark rows in their own style; assumption presets dashed.
modules.human_judgment: Peak scenario choice (event days, train arrival waves), how to trade clear width against trees, patios and seating, perceived crowding by older people and children, and seasonal or weather effects.
modules.limits: TfL comfort levels come from London footway studies; Vancouver conditions differ. Flow comes from assumption presets, not counts. Cyclists, e-scooters and vehicle crossings are not modelled in the static check. Fruin values are unverified.
