modules.name: Inclusive and accessible design at grade
modules.design_question: Can everyone, including wheelchair users, people with low vision and older people, reach and use every public entrance, space and the station link at grade without barriers?
modules.effort: About 5-7 person-days; slope mapping and rest-spacing checks are simple, door and entrance data need annotation. Not in the 13 Nov slice; ships by 10 Dec.
inputs: Terrain: DEM or spot elevations for the site and surrounding streets (SITE packet)
Layer0 ground slab levels, entrances with threshold heights, stairs, ramps and lifts (tagged objects)
P06-M04 RouteGraph, clear widths and below-grade link lifts and stairs
Seating points from P06-M03; crossing and curb-ramp points
Manual fields: door clear width, automatic openers, tactile surfaces, accessible washrooms
outputs: SlopeMap: raster of running slope (%) and crossfall (%)
StepFreeRoutes: {from_entrance, to_target, step_free, max_slope, max_gap_to_rest_m}[]
RestCoverage: polygons within 50 m, 100 m and 150 m of seating
AccessChecks: Check[] (consumed by P06-M08 and PRES)

parameters.name: Running slope of public routes
parameters.relationship: Steeper slope means more effort and need to rest; 5% (1:20) is the City target where achievable, anything steeper is a ramp, and 1:12 is the UK absolute maximum for short runs.

parameters.name: Crossfall
parameters.relationship: Crossfall drains water but makes wheelchairs drift and challenges balance; Vancouver designs 2% (1-4% range), UK guidance prefers 1-2% with 1 in 40 as the maximum.

parameters.name: Level change between sidewalk and slab
parameters.relationship: Bigger grade differences force stairs, ramps or lifts; CDDG says integrate them in the building envelope and keep a visual and physical connection to the public realm.

parameters.name: Clear path width
parameters.relationship: At least 2.0 m lets two wheelchairs pass; 1.5 m lets a wheelchair and a walker pass; 1.0 m at obstacles for no more than 6 m (UK guidance).

parameters.name: Spacing of seats and rest spots
parameters.relationship: Closer rests let more people complete a walk: EDM Table 8-2 gives 150 m for wheelchair and visually impaired users, 100 m for mobility impaired without a walking aid, 50 m for stick users. Granville Street Plan area asks resting spots.

parameters.name: Landings on slopes
parameters.relationship: Level landings at least every 0.5 m of rise, as long as the ramp is wide, give rest points and allow passing.

parameters.name: Headroom under canopies, stairs and soffits
parameters.relationship: Headroom of at least 2.3 m prevents head strikes by people with low vision; undersides of stairs need a barrier below that height.

parameters.name: Tactile surfaces at flush crossings
parameters.relationship: Flush crossings lack a curb cue; Vancouver requires truncated domes where grade break is under 5%, so layout must leave room for paired bracketing.

parameters.name: Governing building code and standards
parameters.relationship: BC Building Code does not apply in Vancouver; the Vancouver Building By-law and CSA B651 govern barrier-free entrances, ramps and doors. Numeric requirements were not opened.

metrics.name: Running slope of public paths
metrics.good: At most 5% (1:20) where achievable.
metrics.bad: Above 5% where flatter is achievable; steeper runs are ramps needing landings and handrails.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] Engineering Design Manual 2026 (5% maximum running slope where achievable).
metrics.method: Slope from DEM or pathway profile along each route segment.

metrics.name: Ramp gradient, landings and headroom
metrics.good: Ramp at most 1:20 preferred, 1:12 (8.3%) absolute maximum; landing for each 0.5 m of rise; headroom at least 2.3 m.
metrics.bad: Steeper than 1:12, longer runs without landing, or headroom below 2.3 m.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.2-4.3: text verified, UK guidance, not adopted by Vancouver; Building By-law and CSA B651 not opened.
metrics.method: Check ramp profiles and soffit heights.

metrics.name: Crossfall
metrics.good: About 2% design, within the EDM 1-4% range.
metrics.bad: Outside 1-4%; amber between 2.5% and 4% on constrained sites (DfT would flag above 2.5%, external comparison).
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] EDM 2026 8.4.3.3 (2%, 1-4% range); DfT s4.3 shown only as a comparison.
metrics.method: Cross slope across the sidewalk from the section.

metrics.name: Clear width of public routes
metrics.good: At least 3.0 m on commercial streets; at least 2.4 m on mid-block links.
metrics.bad: Below 2.4 m (constrained minimum), or below 3.0 m on commercial streets without City Engineer agreement.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] EDM Table 8-3; CDDG S3.8.1. DfT 2.0 m desirable footway is an external comparison.
metrics.method: Minimum clear width per route segment from P06-M04.

metrics.name: Obstacle gaps and footway minimum
metrics.good: Footway at least 2.0 m desirable (1.5 m acceptable); gaps at obstacles at least 1.0 m and no longer than 6 m.
metrics.bad: Below 1.5 m anywhere, or below 1.0 m at obstacles longer than 6 m.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.2: text verified, not adopted by Vancouver.
metrics.method: Scan route segments for obstacle gaps.

metrics.name: Rest spacing by user group (EDM Table 8-2)
metrics.good: Gap between resting spots at most: wheelchair users 150 m; visually impaired 150 m; stick users 50 m; mobility impaired without a walking aid 100 m. Report each group.
metrics.bad: Any gap over its group's distance.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] [CORRECTED r2] EDM 2026 Table 8-2, p.249 (research from the late 1980s; average measures). The earlier 'busy routes 50 m' rule is not in the EDM.
metrics.method: Distance along routes between seating nodes; compare to each Table 8-2 group.

metrics.name: Rest spacing, external comparison
metrics.good: A seat or rest spot at most 50 m apart along busy routes (comparison only).
metrics.bad: Gaps over 150 m.
metrics.basis: [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK] DfT Inclusive Mobility s4.5 (50 m); not adopted by Vancouver.
metrics.method: As above; shown beside the EDM groups.

metrics.name: Step-free public entrances
metrics.good: All primary public entrances and the station link step-free from the sidewalk.
metrics.bad: Any public entrance needing a step or a separate back route.
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] Vancouver Building By-law Part 3.8 and CSA B651 not opened; design intent, to be checked by the code consultant.
metrics.method: Graph routing with step edges removed.

metrics.name: Truncated-dome treatment at flush crossings
metrics.good: Required where grade break between sidewalk and ramp top is under 5%.
metrics.bad: Flush crossing without tactile surface.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] EDM 2026 section 8.4.1.4.
metrics.method: Check each crossing point for grade break and tactile flag.

modules.method: Compute a slope raster from the DEM and site grading, or slope profiles along each route edge from P06-M04. Classify running slope as 0-5% (green), 5-8.3% (amber, ramp) and above 8.3% (red). Measure crossfall from sections. Remove edges with steps from the walk graph to find step-free routes between each public entrance, the sidewalk, the plaza and the station link (lifts kept). Report any entrance with no step-free route. Place seating nodes and compute the longest gap along each route against each Table 8-2 group. Check headroom, landings and tactile domes. Compile code items for the code consultant (Vancouver Building By-law, CSA B651) as a manual checklist, not a computed result.
visualization: Ground-plane slope map with three classes (green up to 5%, amber 5-8.3%, red above 8.3%), small arrows for direction of fall and a legend in percent and ratio.
Rest-coverage overlay: 50 m, 100 m and 150 m radius rings around seating nodes, shaded by user group.
Step-free route traces from each public entrance to the station link, breaks marked with an X and the clause that fails.
Checklist panel with badges linked to EDM clauses; DfT rows in the external-benchmark style; code items as 'needs consultant' chips.
modules.human_judgment: Lived-experience review with the City's disability advisory groups, wayfinding clarity, sensory and cognitive comfort (glare, noise, complexity), dignity of access (no separate back door), and independent accessibility rating such as Rick Hansen Foundation certification (not opened).
modules.limits: Code compliance cannot be proven from a massing model. Slope needs an elevation model; downtown grade data may need City LiDAR. DfT numbers are UK benchmarks. No door, handrail or washroom geometry exists in Layer 0.

parameters.name: Public and cultural share of floor area above the streetwall
parameters.relationship: More public floor area above the podium strengthens the sense that public life reaches up the tower; but each public floor needs separate lifts, security and egress and displaces revenue floors.

parameters.name: Height of the highest public storey
parameters.relationship: A public level near the crown gives skyline and mountain views and a reason to travel up; but the top floors are the most valuable and most exposed to wind.

parameters.name: Vertical gap between public levels
parameters.relationship: Large gaps break the idea that public uses extend vertically; sky lobbies and stacked civic rooms at regular intervals make a legible vertical sequence.

parameters.name: Dedicated public vertical circulation
parameters.relationship: Separate public lifts or escalators keep public access independent of tenants and security, but need lobby space and core area; London policy asks for a separate entrance (not opened).

parameters.name: Street-level public lobby and queue
parameters.relationship: A public lift lobby with its own street frontage makes vertical uses visible and welcoming; its queue can spill onto the sidewalk and cut clear width unless the lobby holds the peak queue.

parameters.name: Access regime and hours
parameters.relationship: Free walk-up access and long hours widen the public; booked or ticketed access narrows it. Sky Garden London is free with a booked ticket, open until midnight; Vancouver Lookout at Harbour Centre is ticketed.

parameters.name: Size and height of interior public space
parameters.relationship: Rooms of at least about 93 m2 and 9.1 m high read as civic spaces (borrowed from the FSR-exclusion condition); lobbies serving principal entries and circulation do not count.

parameters.name: Outdoor public terraces at height
parameters.relationship: Open-air public terraces add views and weather exposure; wind comfort there comes from the CLIM wind module and may limit hours or types of use.

metrics.name: Public or cultural GFA above the streetwall
metrics.good: At least 5% of above-podium GFA (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Below 1% (editable preset).
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy asks, where possible, for community-significant uses such as a public observation deck; no number. VTC brief asks that public-facing uses extend vertically.
metrics.method: Sum GFA of public and cultural_civic storeys above the podium line over total GFA above it.

metrics.name: Distinct public levels above the podium
metrics.good: At least two separated public levels, one in the top quarter of building height (editable preset).
metrics.bad: No public level above the podium.
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] No sourced threshold; the preset follows the brief's vertical continuity intent.
metrics.method: Cluster public storeys; count clusters and note the highest.

metrics.name: Maximum gap between public levels
metrics.good: At most one quarter of total height (editable preset).
metrics.bad: More than one half of total height (editable preset).
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] Placeholder; no sourced rule.
metrics.method: Difference between consecutive public storey heights, plus ground to first and last to roof.

metrics.name: Interior public space quality floor
metrics.good: At least about 93.0 m2 and about 9.1 m clear height, secured by covenant.
metrics.bad: Smaller or lower, or secured only by lease; lobbies for principal entries and circulation are excluded.
metrics.basis: [DERIVED] CDDG S3.3.1 is a condition for FSR exclusion of interior public space, not a quality floor for sky-level rooms; the transfer is ours. Glossary excludes principal-entry lobbies.
metrics.method: Check area and floor-to-ceiling height of tagged public rooms.

metrics.name: Street visibility and access of public uses
metrics.good: Public uses have direct visual and physical access from the sidewalk (street-level lobby or frontage), not only through a tenant lobby. Granville area: podium patios and cultural spaces visible from the street (GL2.1.1).
metrics.bad: Hidden behind tenant lobby or reached only by a service route.
metrics.basis: [VERIFIED TEXT] CDDG G3.3.3 (direct visual and physical access from the sidewalk for interior public space); G3.3.1 invites it in major Business District developments; Granville plan GL2.1.1.
metrics.method: Check each public vertical node for a street-level frontage or lobby tag and a sightline from the sidewalk.

metrics.name: Public-lift queue spill-over
metrics.good: Reported only: peak queue persons and the lobby area that holds them, passed to P06-M05; no sourced pass level.
metrics.bad: Queue area exceeds the lobby and spills onto the sidewalk.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Lift capacity belongs to SYST and MOBI; no sourced queue-area standard opened.
metrics.method: Peak public occupant load per lift cycle over lobby area; compare with sidewalk clear width in M05.

metrics.name: Public access hours and cost at height
metrics.good: Free, open to the public from at least 10:00 to 22:00, seven days (editable preset).
metrics.bad: Office hours only, ticketed, or by invitation.
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] Sky Garden London is free with booking and opens to midnight (precedent); Vancouver Lookout is ticketed (City memo, Apr 2026). The 2002 staff report judged a hotel lobby plus roof garden an inadequate public amenity.
metrics.method: Read access attributes per public node.

metrics.name: Public vertical circulation
metrics.good: Dedicated public lifts or an independent public lobby with its own entrance (preset).
metrics.bad: Public level reached only via tenant lobby.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Based on London Plan Policy D9 intent, not opened (Cloudflare challenge).
metrics.method: Check circulation tags for separation.

modules.method: Read the storey table from Layer 0 and tag each storey by public, cultural or civic programme and area. Identify the podium line from the first tower step-back (shared with P06-M02). Compute public share of floor area above the podium, number and positions of public clusters, vertical gaps, height of the highest public storey, and area and clear height of each interior public room. Read access attributes (free, ticketed, hours, covenant) from each public node and the circulation tags to test separation from tenant lifts and street visibility. Estimate the public-lift queue and pass it to P06-M05. Mark each result verified, team assumption or unverified. Pass public occupant demand to SYST (egress) and MOBI (lift capacity).
visualization: Vertical strip diagram: tower elevation as a column from 0 to total height in metres, one band per storey coloured by programme, public storeys outlined with a heavy stroke, lift lines drawn, markers at the highest public storey and the podium line.
Per-node 24-hour clock-arc showing opening hours and a chip for free, booked or ticketed.
Street-level plan of the public lift lobby with its frontage, queue area and the sidewalk clear width beside it.
Histogram of public GFA per 10-storey band; pass/fail badges linked to CDDG clauses and the preset table; derived rows dashed.
modules.human_judgment: Whether the space is welcoming rather than token, programme curation and cultural content (including Indigenous perspectives, logged in the M08 cultural log, not scored here), cost and security screening, equity of access, management, and safety and egress for large public loads at height.
modules.limits: Threshold presets have no sourced value; only CDDG G3.3.3 and precedents are cited, and the 93 m2 room floor is a derived transfer. Life-safety, lift capacity and wind comfort at height belong to other packets. Access regime is user-entered. CTBUH material was not opened (403).

modules.name: Gehl-type public-life triage: what can be computed and what needs people
modules.design_question: Which of Gehl's twelve public-space quality criteria can the tool compute from the massing, which only through proxies, and which need human audit or field observation, and where does cultural context rest on people alone?
modules.effort: About 4-6 person-days for the triage matrix, count bars, manual audit form and cultural-context log; agent-based public-life prediction is roadmap. Ships by 10 Dec.
inputs: Check outputs of P06-M01 to P06-M07 (pass, amber, fail, not assessed: wind, with source badges)
CLIM: sun, wind, rain-shelter and noise results (if available)
ECOL: tree canopy and planting (if available)
Manual audit form (microscale streetscape audit items, exclusionary-feature checklist) filled by team members
Manual cultural-context log entries (human only)
Optional baseline: public-life counts of the existing site (Gehl-style stationary activity and movement counts)
outputs: CriteriaTriage: {criterion, group, mode: computed | proxy | human | field, pass_n, amber_n, fail_n, not_assessed_n, confidence}[12]
PublicLifeProfile: counts per criterion with computed and judged rows distinguished (no score)
PlaceDiagramMap: mapping of results to four place qualities
CulturalContextLog: entries by type {engagement, naming, art, programme, wayfinding, space review} with rater, date, evidence link, Nation review status (counts only)
Gaps: list of criteria still without evidence (for the policy reflection board)

parameters.name: Roll-up rule (counts only)
parameters.relationship: Showing pass, amber, fail and not-assessed counts per criterion keeps the 40% human-scale jury weight visible without inventing weights between criteria; no validated weighting exists, so no 0-100 score or composite is produced.

parameters.name: Evidence mode per criterion
parameters.relationship: A criterion moves from 'human' to 'proxy' to 'computed' as the tool gains data; shows what remains judgment and keeps the scorecard honest.

parameters.name: Audit item set (microscale audit)
parameters.relationship: Structured audit items (for example MAPS-Global) make human ratings repeatable between raters; reported inter-rater reliability was mostly 'excellent' in a Japanese online-audit study.

parameters.name: Exclusionary-feature checklist
parameters.relationship: Seat dividers, spikes, gates and sloped ledges signal who is unwelcome; auditing them gives a partial, human-rated proxy for 'who is welcome'. CDDG G3.1.1c asks grilles and gates permeable at all hours.

parameters.name: Baseline public-life counts
parameters.relationship: Counts of people moving and staying before and after a design show real effect; they cannot come from a massing model and are post-occupancy or existing-site work.

parameters.name: Cultural-context evidence (human only)
parameters.relationship: More logged, Nation-reviewed evidence (engagement, naming, art, programme, wayfinding) strengthens the case under the 30% cultural-context criterion; computed public-realm checks give none of it, so it is kept apart and never rolled up.

metrics.name: Protection against traffic and accidents
metrics.good: Mode proxy: counts of checks on vehicle and bike crossings (M01), crossing and corner comfort and widths (M05); street speeds need SITE data.
metrics.bad: No evidence entered.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criteria list recalled from Cities for People, not opened.
metrics.method: Count linked check statuses; show mode and confidence; no score.

metrics.name: Protection against crime and violence
metrics.good: Mode proxy: active frontage, transparency, night activation, lighting flag, blank runs and grilles (M01); lighting quality needs human input.
metrics.bad: Long blank runs, no night uses.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criteria list not opened. CDDG G3.1.1 supports passive security by lighting, transparency and activity.
metrics.method: Count linked M01 checks plus manual lighting rating.

metrics.name: Protection against unpleasant sensory experiences (wind, rain, noise, pollution)
metrics.good: Mode proxy until CLIM supplies sourced wind results, then computed for wind; shelter (M01) computed; noise and air need other models. Unassessed wind shows grey, not green.
metrics.bad: Strolling-class wind at seating or no weather protection.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criteria list not opened. CDDG S4.11.1 noise levels cover residential rooms and amenity space only; wind benchmark in M03 is external (Toronto).
metrics.method: Count wind-point and shelter checks incl. not_assessed; mark noise and air as gaps.

metrics.name: Opportunities to walk
metrics.good: Mode computed plus human: clear widths and PCL (M05), slopes (M06), directness (M04); edge quality is human.
metrics.bad: Clear width below standard.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criteria list not opened.
metrics.method: Count linked M04-M06 checks; manual edge rating.

metrics.name: Opportunities to stand and stay
metrics.good: Mode computed plus human: edge depth, plaza edges, seating at edges (M01, M03); quality of the edge zone is human.
metrics.bad: No edge zones or seating at edges.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criteria list not opened.
metrics.method: Count linked M01 and M03 checks; manual edge-zone rating.

metrics.name: Opportunities to sit
metrics.good: Mode computed: seating supply, sun and wind at seating (M03); seat comfort and exclusionary features are human.
metrics.bad: No seating or no sun on seating.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criteria list not opened; seating benchmark is NYC (external).
metrics.method: Count M03 seating, sun and wind checks; audit exclusionary features.

metrics.name: Opportunities to see
metrics.good: Mode proxy: sightlines and transparency (M01, M04), eye-level view shares (M02), optional isovist; view-cone status as context (CDDG 4.10); interest of views is human.
metrics.bad: Blocked sightlines or blank edges.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criteria list not opened.
metrics.method: Count linked checks; optional isovist area from key points.

metrics.name: Opportunities to hear and talk
metrics.good: Mode human or field: needs an acoustic model or on-site observation.
metrics.bad: No evidence entered.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criteria list not opened; no public-realm noise threshold found.
metrics.method: Manual audit entries only.

metrics.name: Opportunities to play and exercise
metrics.good: Mode human: programme and facilities are judgments; POPS size and shape (M03) are inputs only.
metrics.bad: No evidence entered.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criteria list not opened.
metrics.method: Manual audit entries; link M03 geometry as context.

metrics.name: Scale
metrics.good: Mode computed plus human: podium band, unit rhythm, massing variation (M01, M02); eye-level view shares (M02) as proxy; perception needs a human check.
metrics.bad: Podium outside the band or unit frontage beyond range.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criterion wording not opened; linked CDDG checks are verified. Gehl dictionary (opened) defines human scale as dimensions relating to the human body and eye-level experience.
metrics.method: Count linked M01 and M02 checks; manual perception rating.

metrics.name: Opportunities to enjoy positive aspects of climate
metrics.good: Mode computed plus human: sun hours (M03), shelter (M01), wind class, UTCI from CLIM if offered; trees from ECOL; comfort in use is human.
metrics.bad: Shaded, windy plaza with no planting.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criteria list not opened; PPS Place Diagram lists sun or shade under comfort and image.
metrics.method: Count M03 sun, M01 shelter and wind checks; manual rating.

metrics.name: Positive sensory experiences
metrics.good: Mode human: materials, detailing, views and planting quality; ECOL canopy is an input only.
metrics.bad: No evidence entered.
metrics.basis: [UNVERIFIED] Criteria list not opened.
metrics.method: Manual audit entries; link ECOL canopy as context.

metrics.name: Share of criteria with computed or proxy evidence
metrics.good: Reported as a count out of 12; preset target at least 6 of 12 by 10 Dec 2026.
metrics.bad: Fewer than 4 of 12.
metrics.basis: [TEAM ASSUMPTION] Project management measure, not a design threshold.
metrics.method: Count criteria whose mode is computed or proxy.

metrics.name: Cultural-context evidence log (30% criterion; human only)
metrics.good: Dated human entries: engagement with Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations (who, when, outcome), naming and wayfinding, art and programme, review of Indigenous-named Table 1 spaces. Counts by type; no score.
metrics.bad: Reconciliation claimed from computed checks, or no log.
metrics.basis: [HUMAN-JUDGMENT PROTOCOL] CDDG has a land acknowledgement (p.10) and introduction (p.16) but no Indigenous design standard in its body. VTC brief wording not re-opened (site returned 502).
metrics.method: Manual log form: type, rater initials, date, evidence link, Nation review status. Counts per type only; never fed by M01-M07 scores.

modules.method: Create a 12-row matrix, one row per criterion, grouped protection (3), comfort (6) and delight (3). For each row record the evidence mode (computed, proxy, human audit, field observation) and link the module checks used. Pull checks from P06-M01 to P06-M07 and show pass, amber, fail and not-assessed counts with source badges. Never convert to 0-100 or a composite: the 40% human-scale weight stays at category level. For human rows present a short microscale audit form with rater initials, date and an exclusionary-feature checklist. Draw counts per row, computed rows solid and judged rows hatched. Cross-map to the PPS Place Diagram. Keep the cultural-context log as a separate human-only panel, not a thirteenth row. Mark the criteria list UNVERIFIED until Cities for People or another Gehl source is opened.
visualization: Twelve rows grouped protection, comfort and delight; each row a stacked bar of pass, amber, fail and not-assessed counts; computed rows solid, proxy dotted, human hatched, field-only empty with a dashed ring; no total.
Triage matrix: rows are criteria, columns are computed / proxy / human audit / field data, with the source module and clause linked in each cell.
Four-quadrant Place Diagram overlay (access and linkages, uses and activities, comfort and image, sociability) with counts of evidence per quadrant.
Separate cultural-context panel: entry counts by type, human-only badge; badge 'Human-scale experience: 40% of jury' on the profile; FALSE ASSUMPTION colour for any retracted rating.
modules.human_judgment: Almost all 'delight' criteria, edge quality, seat comfort, perceived safety, who feels welcome, noise tolerance, cultural meaning and inclusion. Engagement with the three Nations is done by people, not by the tool. Field counts and surveys need a built or existing place.
modules.limits: Gehl's criteria wording and any quantity were recalled, not opened, so no Gehl numbers are thresholds. No validated composite exists. Proxies measure the model, not behaviour; counts of people need field work. The cultural log records evidence; it does not judge reconciliation.

sources.extract: Text read: Table 3 comfort (GEM 10, 15, 20 km/h at 80% of 6:00-23:00; uncomfortable above 20 at 20%) and safety (gust above 90 km/h, 0.1% of hours); four seasons; areas of interest; wind control strategies (setbacks, podiums, corners, canopies).

sources.title: RTS 18459 Appendix C, Table 10: Granville Street Plan, new Section 3 Urban Design Framework (pp.38-39)
sources.extract: Read r2 (PDF pp.153-154): 24/7 destination; lighting, clear sight lines, inclusive features; queuing areas and resting spots; towers complement fine grain; GL1.2.x venue entrances; GL2.1.x podium patios visible, entertainment above or below ground floor; screens dimmed after 10 pm.

sources.title: Measuring Perceived Psychological Stress in Urban Built Environments Using Google Street View and Deep Learning (Han et al.; accessed through PubMed)
sources.publisher: Frontiers in Public Health (indexed in PubMed)
sources.extract: According to PubMed: Seoul Gangnam street-view study; segmentation of view elements; walls and buildings associated with higher perceived stress, sky, trees and roads with lower. Direction only; no transferable threshold.

sources.title: Exploring the spatial association between the distribution of temperature and urban morphology with green view index (Chan et al.; accessed through PubMed)
sources.extract: According to PubMed: semantic segmentation of Google Street View gives green view index, building view factor and sky view factor at pedestrian level in Taipei; method precedent for eye-level view shares, not a threshold.

sources.title: A review on the study of urban wind at the pedestrian level around buildings (Mittal, Sharma and Gairola; accessed through PubMed)
sources.publisher: Journal of Building Engineering (indexed in PubMed)
sources.extract: According to PubMed: reviews assessment methods and different wind comfort criteria; finds a strong need to homogenise criteria; wind comfort for high and low speeds matters; corner modification, lift-up and podiums are positive design approaches.

sources.title: Pedestrians' behavior based on outdoor thermal comfort and micro-scale thermal environments, Austin, TX (Kim and Brown; accessed through PubMed)
sources.publisher: Science of the Total Environment (indexed in PubMed)
sources.extract: According to PubMed: in downtown Austin pedestrians chose walking, sitting and standing places with high thermal comfort, such as shaded sidewalk; sky view factor and tree canopy ratio correlated with thermal comfort. Supports reporting a thermal layer, not a threshold.

sources.title: Pedestrian wind comfort near a super-tall building with various configurations in an urban-like setting (Zhang et al.; accessed through PubMed)
sources.extract: According to PubMed: CFD of a 400 m tower in 50 m context; square plan raised maximum mean wind speed 1.53 times and cut area with acceptable comfort; rounded plans, corner modifications, tapered and setback shapes helped in windy climate.

flags.claim: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy is the policy that frames 244-305 m (800-1,000 ft) towers on the VTC site.
flags.correction: The City's April 2026 memo says the policy was last updated in 2011 and currently allows up to 600 ft (about 183 m), with one location up to 700 ft (about 213 m). The VTC height range is above it. The review is open and draft directions are expected in late 2026.
flags.detail: Sources: P06-S04, P06-S03. VTC heights are hypothetical beyond current policy; the 1997 criteria on public amenity, open space and microclimate (P06-S05) are used here as the policy intent.

flags.claim: The Downtown (Except Downtown South) Design Guidelines and Central Area Pedestrian Weather Protection guidelines govern podium, streetwall and ground-floor design for Central Business District sites.
flags.correction: Council approved the City-wide Design and Development Guidelines on 28 July 2026 and repealed both documents effective 27 October 2026. The CDDG now governs; its final text was not yet posted. CDDG 4.18 still refers Downtown sites to the DD Character Area Descriptions.
flags.detail: Sources: P06-S01 (Appendix B, 4.18), P06-S02. Use CDDG clause numbers, not legacy guideline numbers, in all source badges.

flags.claim: Vancouver requires a numeric ground-floor transparency percentage.
flags.correction: The CDDG asks for transparent glazing across most of the ground-floor facade up to the second-floor underside or canopy underside, with no percentage. Any percentage in the tool is a team assumption.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S01 (S3.1.1b).

flags.claim: Downtown solar rules prohibit any new shadow on all public spaces between 10:00 and 16:00 PDT.
flags.correction: The Downtown Peninsula guidelines are tiered: no new shadow on parks, school sites and the Davie and Robson Village north sidewalks; urban plazas and miniparks to be minimised; exceptions through a rationale, 15-minute solar budget and detailed study. Time wording amended from PDT to PT on 28 July 2026.
flags.detail: Sources: P06-S09, P06-S01 (Appendix D), P06-S10.

flags.claim: New shadow on urban plazas only needs to be 'actively minimised' (P06-M03 protected-space metric).
flags.correction: Dilawri Square South, Jack Poole Plaza and Robson Square follow 3.1 (no new shadow, 22 Sep, 10:00-16:00, exception path 3.1.2). Dr Sun Yat-Sen Gardens and Park: no new shadow 10:00-16:00 (4.1.1). Victory Square: 3.1 plus the Cenotaph circle 10:00-12:00 on 11 Nov (4.3.1). Other urban plazas and West End miniparks: minimise where possible (3.2.1).
flags.detail: Source: P06-S09 Appendix A (clean text) sections 3.1-3.3, 4.1-4.3, Table 1. The earlier packet read the redline, which mixes struck and inserted text.

flags.claim: Vancouver's shadow test is the 10:00-16:00 run in 15-minute steps.
flags.correction: Every Downtown applicant submits a Basic study at two-hour intervals (5.1.1). The 15-minute Detailed study with area take-offs and the coverage formula is for applicants seeking a relaxation of 3.1.1 or 3.3.1 (5.2.1).
flags.detail: Source: P06-S09 Appendix A section 5. The tool offers both studies, Basic by default.

flags.claim: The 10% public open space target for mid-sized sites (S1.9.2) is a valid passing target for the VTC block.
flags.correction: S1.9.2 does not apply: the CDDG glossary defines mid-sized sites as over 4,000 and under 8,000 m2, and the VTC block is about 11,468 m2. Default to S1.9.1 (20%), with POPS of about 10% (S1.10.2) counted inside it.
flags.detail: Sources: P06-S01 (glossary, S1.9.1, S1.9.2, S1.10.2), P06-S37 (large-site trigger 8,000 m2 in the 2013 report; current policy not opened).

flags.claim: Mid-block connections of 5.4 m (non-residential), 7.3 m or 4.5 m (half share) are acceptable on the VTC block.
flags.correction: S1.12.2c requires 9.1 m face to face for large sites or sites identified in S1.12.1, and S1.12.1b covers sites adjacent to or including a transit station entrance, which the VTC brief requires. Narrower widths only as a G1.12.1 variation.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S01 (S1.12.1, S1.12.2, G1.12.1, S3.8.1). Checked in the CDDG text in r1.

flags.claim: CDDG Table 1.5 tower separation is employment-employment 15.2, employment-hotel 15.2, employment-residential 18.3 and residential-residential 24.4 m.
flags.correction: The table also sets residential-hotel at 24.4 m (reducible to 18.3 m under S1.5.2) and hotel-hotel at 15.2 m; G1.5.1 asks for more separation where towers exceed typical heights. Use the full matrix with S1.5.2 and S1.5.3 conditions.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S01 (S1.5.1-S1.5.4, G1.5.1-G1.5.2, Table 1.5). Separation is shared equally between tower sites (S1.5.1). r2: full matrix confirmed in the PDF render.

flags.claim: CDDG S2.2.8 allows 21.3 m podiums only for residential or other listed exceptions.
flags.correction: S2.2.8b also allows 21.3 m on sites with frontage over 60.7 m where enhanced open space is provided; the VTC block frontage (79.2 m and 144.8 m) meets the frontage test.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S01 (S2.2.7, S2.2.8, glossary 'Enhanced open space'). Which of S2.2.6 or S2.2.7 governs a mixed tower was unresolved in r1; resolved in r2, see the r2 flag on S2.2.7.

flags.claim: Transport interchanges and tourist areas tolerate less crowding than residential streets (TfL).
flags.correction: TfL Figure 9: high street and tourist attraction are strictest (acceptable to B, at risk B-, unacceptable from C+); residential is intermediate (acceptable to B-, at risk C+); office/retail and transport interchange are most tolerant (acceptable to C+, at risk C-). B+ is recommended for all; C+ is the floor with compensation.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S16 p.14. Read from the figure's colour fills by pixel sampling; the round-1 critic's reading (high street most tolerant) does not match, so a visual check is advised. r2: vector fills and column notes confirm the spec's reading.

flags.claim: TfL Appendix B gives 5.3 m total footway width for any flow above 1,200 pph.
flags.correction: TfL says 5.3 m (or 3.3 m without furniture) gives comfortable movement up to 2,000 pph. Above that, derive the clear width from ppmm at B+ (pph / 60 / 11) plus buffers.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S16 Appendix B (p.25), text read.

flags.claim: Solar tests run in 'local Pacific time', with seasonal PST/PDT switching.
flags.correction: Council report RTS 18459 states BC adopted permanent year-round daylight-saving time, and Appendix D replaces PDT with PT. The guidelines set the model to PDT (UTC-7). Use UTC-7 year-round and show the offset; Victory Square 4.3.1 still says PST (unresolved).
flags.detail: Sources: P06-S01 p.5 and Appendix D, P06-S09 section 5.

flags.claim: The City EDM requires street furniture at least 1.0 m from vehicle crossings and entrances.
flags.correction: No 1.0 m figure was found in EDM 8.4.3, 8.4.9 or Chapter 9. EDM p.341 asks furniture to be set back to keep sightlines at driveways and crosswalks, typically 10 m from intersections.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S11. The 1.0 m figure is removed; no replacement number is claimed.

flags.claim: The S2.2.7 18.3 m Downtown podium cap applies to a mixed-use tower whenever residential floors sit above, and which of S2.2.6 or S2.2.7 governs a mixed tower is unresolved (P06-M02).
flags.correction: For the VTC tower use Table 2.2b (S2.2.6); apply S2.2.7 only to exclusively residential towers. S2.2.8b raises Table 2.2b maxima below 21.3 m to 21.3 m on frontage over 60.7 m with enhanced open space; ROW over 30.5 m already allows 23.0 m, so 21.3 m is no cap there.
flags.detail: Glossary: 'Residential development' = exclusively residential uses or choice-of-use at grade; S2.2.7 covers podiums 'associated with residential developments'. Table 2.2b is titled for mixed-use and non-residential developments. Source: P06-S01 Appendix A pp.25-26, glossary. S2.2.8 as increase-only is our reading.

flags.claim: CDDG G4.4.1 (station overbuild and plaza checklist) applies only where a development includes a station overbuild or primary headhouse; the VTC brief may not include one (P06-M04).
flags.correction: G4.4.2a says integrated station entrances must meet the form and massing guidelines for overbuild and plaza fit-out in 4.4.1, so the VTC's required secondary entrance triggers the G4.4.1 a-h checklist (overbuild-dependent items 'where feasible').
flags.detail: Source: P06-S01 Appendix A p.69 (G4.4.1 a-h, G4.4.2 a-e, S4.4.1).

flags.claim: A building's shadow polygon is the convex hull of its footprint and the footprint shifted by H / tan(elevation) (P06-M03 method).
flags.correction: Project each constant-footprint slab at its own height (footprint swept from base to top along the shadow direction: both end polygons plus swept edge parallelograms), union all slabs and context, then intersect with protected spaces; validate against ray casts on a stepped massing.
flags.detail: Valid only for a convex prism of uniform height. For podium plus 305 m tower it sweeps the whole podium plan (about 79-145 m) to tower height, and fills concave plans, so shadow is overstated along a 600 m to 1.4 km reach and could falsely fail parks. Our geometry.

flags.claim: The Granville Street Plan referred to by CDDG 4.18 was not available, so its content is unknown (P06-S40).
flags.correction: RTS 18459 Appendix C pp.38-39 reproduces the plan's new Urban Design Framework: 24/7 destination; lighting, clear sight lines, inclusive features; queuing areas and resting spots; transit entries; screens dimmed after 22:00; towers that complement the fine grain. The DD character area descriptions remain unopened.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S42 (PDF pp.153-154). 4.18 sends Downtown sites outside the Granville Street Plan area, Downtown South and the West End to the DD descriptions; the plan area to the Granville Street Plan.

flags.claim: TfL Figure 9 shows the high street as the most crowding-tolerant area type, and average-of-maximum guidance differs only for interchange (round-1 critic's claim; spec carried a 'confirm visually' caveat).
flags.correction: Figure 9: high street and tourist are strictest and use the same guidance for peak and average-of-maximum; residential, office/retail and interchange relax 'at risk' in the average-of-maximum column. Spec ordering was right; caveat dropped.
flags.detail: Decoded in r2 from vector fills and page text (P06-S16 p.14): peak acceptable to B (high street, tourist), B- (residential), C+ (office/retail, interchange); average-of-maximum at risk C+ to C- (residential), C- to D (office/retail, interchange).

flags.claim: EDM Table 8-2 asks for a seat or rest spot every 50 m along busy routes (P06-M06 rest spacing).
flags.correction: Table 8-2 gives maximum distances between resting spots by user group: wheelchair users 150 m, visually impaired 150 m, mobility impaired with a stick 50 m, without a walking aid 100 m. The busy-route 50 m rule belongs to DfT, as an external comparison.
flags.detail: Source: P06-S11 p.249 (re-read r2; research from the late 1980s, average measures).

flags.claim: Computed P06 checks (M03, M06, M07) evidence the 30% cultural-context jury criterion.
flags.correction: No computed P06 check measures reconciliation or cultural context. It is a human-judgment record (M08 cultural-context log). M03 only names Indigenous-named Table 1 spaces and routes them to human review.
flags.detail: CDDG body (pp.17-100) has no Indigenous design clause; only a land acknowledgement (p.10) and introduction (p.16). Source: P06-S01. cultural_context_30 removed from M06 and M07.

flags.claim: CDDG clause values (entrances, podium bands, tower separation, floorplates, open space targets) are final.
flags.detail: The only text read is draft Appendix A in the Council report. The City says final guidelines will be posted. Tables 2.2b and 1.5 were checked against page renders in r2, but recheck every CDDG number after posting.

flags.claim: Gehl door-density scale, viewing-distance limits and the wording of the twelve quality criteria.
flags.detail: The Gehl People site, its dictionary and Wikipedia do not list the criteria; the book was not opened. No Gehl figure is used as a threshold; criteria names are recalled and flagged. City entrance spacing (8-12 m) is the verified substitute.

flags.claim: Fruin and Highway Capacity Manual pedestrian level-of-service values.
flags.detail: Not opened. The tool uses TfL Pedestrian Comfort Levels (opened) as the primary measure and shows Fruin only as an unverified cross-check.

flags.claim: BC and Vancouver accessibility code requirements (Vancouver Building By-law Part 3.8, CSA B651) for entrances, ramps and doors.
flags.detail: The BC page says BC codes do not apply in Vancouver; the by-law text and CSA standard were not opened. Numeric accessibility metrics come from the City EDM and the UK DfT guide.

flags.claim: London Plan Policy D9 requirement for free-to-enter public space at height.
flags.detail: The London Authority site blocked access. The policy is not used for any number; it appears only as a flagged reference.

flags.claim: Pedestrian wind comfort and safety criteria at grade for Vancouver (seating, entrances, sidewalks, transit plaza, links, terraces).
flags.detail: No Vancouver numeric criterion found; CDDG G1.8.1b is qualitative. r2: Toronto's 2022 guide (P06-S41, Table 3) opened as an external benchmark; a review finds wind criteria differ between jurisdictions (P06-S45, abstract). CLIM confirms or replaces; until then badges read 'not assessed: wind'.

flags.claim: Current text of the Rezoning Policy for Sustainable Large Developments (large-site trigger).
flags.detail: The policy PDF returned 403 again in r2. The 8,000 m2 site or 45,000 m2 floor-area trigger is read in the 2013 Council report only (P06-S37); the VTC block (11,468 m2) meets the site test on that text.

flags.claim: Availability of pvlib, trimesh, momepy and OSMnx inside Pyodide.
flags.detail: They were not in the built-in package list read (P06-S39); installing pure-Python wheels with micropip is untested. The browser path relies only on shapely, numpy and scipy plus an own solar routine; trimesh ray-cast validation runs server-side or in a test harness.

flags.claim: Orthography of Indigenous-named Table 1 spaces and of the Nations' names.
flags.detail: Names were read from the PDF text layer (P06-S09 Table 1; CDDG p.10), which splits diacritics; the round-2 critic's spelling of the Rainbow Park name differs by one vowel. Import strings from City data and check glyph by glyph before any display.

flags.claim: Eye-level view shares and sky-patch settings as predictors of perceived enclosure.
flags.detail: Ewing and Handy 2009 not opened; two street-view studies read as abstracts only (P06-S43, P06-S44), from Seoul and Taipei. Elevation bands (0-15, 15-30, 30-60, 60-90 degrees) and at least 2,000 patches are team presets; no threshold is claimed.

flags.claim: Which VTC frontages are retail-continuity streets under the Downtown District ODP, and which character area or plan governs the block.
flags.detail: The ODP map sits on bylaws.vancouver.ca and could not be read. CDDG 4.18 sends Downtown sites to the DD C-5, C-6, HA-1 or HA-2 descriptions (not opened) or, in its area, to the Granville Street Plan (framework text read in r2). The user selects the policy area in SITE.

flags.claim: Whether the VTC block (about 11,468 m2) counts as a 'large site' for the 20% public open space target, and how S1.9.1 and S1.10.2 stack.
flags.detail: Glossary sends large sites to the Rezoning Policy for Sustainable Large Developments (403 again) and unique sites to the area plan; the 2013 report gives an 8,000 m2 trigger, which the block meets. POPS is a public open space (glossary), so it counts inside the 20%; whether S1.10.2 is extra is unconfirmed.

flags.claim: Status and timing of the Higher Buildings Policy review.
flags.detail: The April 2026 memo gives the Ideas Competition as June 2026 to January 2027; the City page says live until 30 November 2026. Phase 2 draft directions are expected late 2026, so thresholds may change after this packet.

flags.claim: Applying CDDG low-rise streetwall Table 2.2a (east-west versus north-south streets) on the rotated downtown grid.
flags.detail: The tower-podium table 2.2b does not depend on orientation, so the tool uses it. The low-rise table and corner-setback guideline (G2.1.3) need a rule for 'north-south' on a rotated grid.

flags.claim: Time zone of the Victory Square Cenotaph rule (4.3.1 says PST) when BC uses permanent daylight time.
flags.detail: Appendix D replaces PDT with PT but leaves 'PST' in 4.3.1. At 10:00 on 11 Nov the sun is 12.6 degrees up at UTC-7 and 18.3 at UTC-8; the tool runs both until the City confirms.

flags.claim: Whether the 3.1.2 exception path applies to Dr Sun Yat-Sen Gardens and Park (4.1.1).
flags.detail: 4.1.1 says 'despite' 3.1 and states no exception. The tool marks it FAIL with no exception chip; ask City planners.

flags.claim: Whether S3.9.1 (at least 50% of enhanced open space planted with trees) applies to a non-residential tower site, and how it sits with a paved plaza or POPS.
flags.detail: S3.9 is titled for densifying residential neighbourhoods; S2.2.8b invokes 'enhanced open space', which the glossary defines as at-grade public open space free of overhead buildings. The tool reports planted share and applies the 50% rule as a team assumption.

flags.claim: Which wind comfort and safety criterion set CLIM adopts for Vancouver, and who owns the wind result before 13 Nov.
flags.detail: Toronto 2022 Table 3 is the opened external benchmark; Lawson-type and other sets were not opened. Until CLIM names its document and supplies a result, M01, M03 and M04 grade-level badges stay 'not assessed: wind'.

flags.claim: How the 30% cultural-context criterion is evidenced for the public realm, who engages Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh, and when.
flags.detail: The CDDG body has no Indigenous design standard; the VTC brief wording was not re-opened (502). M08 keeps a human-only evidence log; the team must decide ownership and Nation-led review before 10 Dec.

flags.claim: Active-frontage percentages, transparency 60%, blank-run lengths, weather-protection coverage, streetwall continuity 80%, active depth 9.1 m, lobby class defaults.
flags.detail: Editable presets in P06-M01 and P06-M02 without a Vancouver numeric source; the 9.1 m depth borrows G2.10.2c as an analogue; office and residential lobbies default semi-active. Shown dashed with an editable chip.

flags.claim: Sun test of 2 hours on 50% of POPS area, access-hour presets, route directness 1.25/1.5, 100 m block-gap, two lifts on the below-grade link, vertical-public presets (5% GFA, two levels, gap, 10:00-22:00), pedestrian generation rates.
flags.detail: Editable presets in P06-M03, P04, P05 and P07; the 2-hour test is a labelled analogue of unopened BRE practice moved from 21 March to 22 Sep.

flags.claim: Walking speed for isochrones, peak-hour share of daily trips, peak 15-minute surge proxy and low/central/high demand multipliers.
flags.detail: Editable defaults; Transportation 2040 (two-thirds of trips on foot, bike or transit by 2040) is context only. TfL's average of maximum (busiest 10-second samples) has no published hourly conversion.

flags.claim: Status mapping: external benchmarks and derived values are stored as team_assumption with a tag in the basis text.
flags.detail: The output schema allows only verified, team_assumption, unverified and false_assumption_corrected. r2: every basis starts with [VERIFIED TEXT], [EXTERNAL BENCHMARK], [DERIVED], [TEAM ASSUMPTION], [UNVERIFIED] or [HUMAN-JUDGMENT PROTOCOL], plus [CORRECTED r1/r2]. Rows corrected only in r1 now show their evidence status. Recommend adding external_benchmark, derived and corrected_in_round fields to the platform.

flags.claim: Performance budget: protected-space shadow projection for 25 instants and about 200 context buildings completes in under 30 s in a laptop browser.
flags.detail: Not benchmarked; per-slab projection (r2) multiplies polygon work by the number of height slabs. Use few slabs for context buildings and cache by instant. Polygon projection still replaces a 0.5 m ray grid (about 23 million cells per instant at 1.35 km).

flags.claim: 13 Nov working-core slice for P06 is about 12 person-days: M01 about 3, M02 about 3, M03 about 4, M04 about 1.5, wind badge state about 0.5.
flags.detail: Our estimate. Two students have about 17 working days (22 Oct to 13 Nov, our count), about 34 person-days if full time; 12 is about 35% of that, for one of 13 categories. Team must confirm the share or cut further; M05-M08, M03 Detailed and sun raster move to 10 Dec.

flags.claim: Eye-level view bands, 2,000-patch sky sampling, shadow-validation tolerance (grid discretisation bound) and extra own-POPS sun windows (for example 21 Jun and 21 Mar, 11:30-14:00).
flags.detail: Team presets added in r2, editable and shown dashed; none has a Vancouver source. City may ask other dates (solar guideline 3.1.4).

unresolved_relationships: Quantified link between active-frontage percentage or entrance density and pedestrian volume, dwell time and perceived safety: no opened source (Gehl, Ewing and Handy 2009 not opened).

Podium height, canopy and step-back geometry to ground-level wind downwash and sidewalk sunlight: direction is supported (Toronto guide, one CFD abstract) but no opened source gives a Vancouver threshold or effect size; belongs to CLIM.

Acceptable level of sky view factor, enclosure ratio or eye-level view shares on a downtown street: only CDDG-derived podium ratios (about 0.55-0.75) and two street-view abstracts (direction only) are available; no threshold opened.
Acceptable share of added shadow area: staff say 5-15% is typical for high-rises but explicitly set no benchmark; the tool treats any added shadow on no-new-shadow spaces as a breach.
Effect of public floors at height on lift demand, security cost and revenue: no opened source; London D9 and CTBUH material not opened.
Pedestrian generation rates by programme and walk share for the VTC site, and the surge multiplier from hourly flow to peak 15 minutes or TfL average-of-maximum: no Vancouver source opened.
Vancouver hours-of-access rule for POPS under SRW agreements; only the NYC rule was opened.
Route directness and block-length thresholds that predict walking; only a connectivity-physical activity association (children) was opened.
Wind comfort and safety thresholds for Vancouver at seating, entrances, sidewalks, transit plaza, links and terraces: Toronto 2022 benchmark opened (external); CLIM must confirm or replace it.
Whether CDDG S1.10.2 (POPS about 10%) is extra to or inside S1.9.1 (20%), and how park dedication interacts; glossary counts POPS as public open space.
Whether S3.9.1 (50% planted with trees) governs the enhanced open space that unlocks the S2.2.8b 21.3 m podium on a non-residential tower site.
Required width, daylight and lift count of the below-grade station link relative to ridership: CDDG gives only 'an elevator and staircase'; TransLink standards not opened.
Effect of tower separation beyond Table 1.5 on light reaching the pedestrian level for 244-305 m towers: G1.5.1 is qualitative; no number found.
Meaning of PT versus PST for the Victory Square Cenotaph window under permanent daylight time (UTC-7 or UTC-8).
Public-lift queue length and area per person at street level, and its effect on sidewalk comfort: no sourced standard (Fruin queueing values not opened).

How cultural context (reconciliation with Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh) is evidenced for the public realm: no CDDG clause, no computed proxy; human log only, engagement owner and timing undecided.
Whether permanent protected view cones (CDDG 4.10, Public Views Guidelines not opened) constrain the tower footprint or height on the VTC block.
change_log: R1: Created packet P06 with eight modules: ground-floor frontage (M01), streetwall and enclosure (M02), public open space with sun, wind link and access (M03), permeability (M04), sidewalk capacity and pedestrian comfort (M05), inclusive access at grade (M06), vertical public realm (M07), Gehl-type public-life triage (M08).
R1: Servicing and loading frontage impact folded into M01 (service share, vehicle crossings); Gehl indicators placed in M08 as a computed-versus-judged matrix.

R1: Read the City-wide Design and Development Guidelines (draft Appendix A in Council report RTS 18459, 28 Jul 2026) as the governing guideline from 27 Oct 2026; flagged legacy downtown guidelines as repealed.
R1: Corrected the 'Higher Buildings Policy 1997' assumption: last updated 2011, caps about 183 m (one site 213 m), review open.
R1: Built sun metrics on the Downtown Peninsula solar guidelines (22 Sep, 10:00-16:00, 15-minute steps, coverage formula) and amended PDT to PT wording.

R1: Could not open guidelines.vancouver.ca, bylaws.vancouver.ca, london.gov.uk, tandfonline, Gehl sites or BRE; used same-site Council and City PDFs instead; web search budget was exhausted, so remaining gaps are listed as unresolved.

r1: M03 shadow rules rebuilt as rows from solar memo Appendix A: parks and school sites (3.1), Dr Sun Yat-Sen (4.1), Dilawri South, Jack Poole, Robson Square (4.2), Victory Square plus Cenotaph on 11 Nov (4.3), Davie and Robson sidewalks (3.3); no-new-shadow spaces FAIL by default with an exception path; other plazas 'minimise' (3.2.1). FALSE_ASSUMPTION flagged.

r1: M03 offers Basic (2-hour) and Detailed (15-minute, City coverage formula) studies; context now includes proposed buildings and terrain; UTC-7 hard-coded with offset shown; Victory Square PST flagged UNRESOLVED and run at both offsets.

r1: M03 shadow domain sized from tower height (about 600 m on 22 Sep, 1.4 km on 11 Nov at 305 m, our NOAA calculation); protected-space take-offs switched to shapely shadow-polygon projection in the browser; raster only for on-site POPS; sun hours integrated over 24 intervals (max 6.0 h).

r1: M03 open space default set to 20% (S1.9.1) with POPS about 10% (S1.10.2) inside it, per glossary; mid-sized 10% option removed; large-site trigger read in the 2013 Council report only, flagged UNVERIFIED for current text.
